Who are they? These are my two nieces.
And this is my aunt, and this is my uncle.
Who's in your family, Tim?
This is my wife.
These are my parents: my mum and dad.
These are my grandparents: my grandma and grandpa.
And this is my aunt and uncle.
Do you have any brothers or sisters?
Yes, I have one older brother, and two sisters: One older sister and one younger sister.
Who are they? This is my niece and my nephew.

title: Clothes shopping: "Do you have this in a smaller size?"
sourceTitle: Talking about clothes shopping: Easy English Conversations Episode 19
description: Mua quần áo: How do these shoes look? They're a bit big. Do you have them in a smaller size / in black? I'll take them.

segments.text: I need to do some shopping too.
What do you need?
I need some shoes and some gloves.
How do these shoes look?
Hmm. They look a bit big.
Do they have them in a smaller size?
Excuse me. Yes. These shoes are a bit big.
Do you have them in a smaller size?
Yes, we do. How are these?
They are much better.
What else do you need?
I need some gloves.
How about these? How do these gloves look, Tim?
Have they got them in black?
Do you have these in black?
Yes, we do. They're much better.
I'll take them. What do you need, Georgie?
I need some trousers and some socks.
How do these trousers look?
They look a bit small.
Do they have them in a larger size?
I'll ask. Excuse me.
Yes? Do you have these in a larger size?
Yes, we do. How are these?
They're much better. I'll take them.
What else do you need?
I need some socks.
How are these? Do they have them in purple?
Do you have these in purple?
Yes we do. They're perfect.

title: What do I need in my new home?
sourceTitle: Describing your home: Easy English Conversations Episode 20
description: Georgie có nhà mới nhưng trống trơn! Từ vựng đồ đạc: bed, lamp, wardrobe, drawers, fridge, cupboards, oven, microwave.

segments.text: This is the bedroom.
What furniture do I need?
You need a bed.
A bed. You need a lamp.
A lamp. You need a bedside table.
A bedside table. And you need a wardrobe.
A wardrobe. Thanks. So, I've got a bed, a lamp, a table, and a wardrobe in my bedroom.
This is the dining room.
What furniture do I need here?
You need a table.
A table. You need four chairs.
Four chairs. And you need some drawers.
Drawers. Thanks! So, I've got a table, four chairs, and some drawers in my dining room.
This is the kitchen.
What do I need here?
You need a fridge.
A fridge. You need some cupboards.
Cupboards. You need an oven.
An oven. And you need a microwave.
A microwave. So, I've got a fridge, some cupboards, an oven, and a microwave in my kitchen.

title: What's your friend like?
sourceTitle: How to talk about personality in English! Easy English Conversations Episode 16
description: Tả tính cách: grumpy, brave, talkative, quiet, hardworking, lazy — và cách nói từ trái nghĩa "the opposite of…".

segments.text: Hi, Tim. Hello. Who's this?
This is my friend, Tom.
What's your friend like?
He's not friendly. He's quite grumpy.
He's usually angry or annoyed about something!
But I'm also brave.
I like extreme sports like bungee jumping, skydiving, and rock climbing.
Wow, that is brave.
Tom sounds like my friend, Gina!
What is Gina like?
She is sporty, and she is talkative.
Talkative. Tom isn't talkative.
He's the opposite of talkative.
He's quiet. He doesn't talk very much.
Sounds like Shannon! She's quiet.
She's also hardworking. Hardworking?
Tom isn't hardworking. He's the opposite of hardworking.
He's lazy. He sits on the sofa a lot and watches TV.

title: How do you take your coffee?
sourceTitle: How do you take your coffee? Real Easy English
description: Neil và Georgie trò chuyện về cà phê: take your coffee black/white, decaf, caffeine, cut down on — rất tự nhiên.

segments.text: So, Georgie, we're talking about coffee.
How much coffee, or how many coffees if we're talking about cups of coffee – how many do you have a day?
I usually have two, and I know that you do as well, because we drink them both in the office, don't we?
We have one cup of coffee in the morning and one usually in the afternoon, when we need to regain some energy and alertness.
Yeah. And so, we all know because we make each other...
at BBC Learning English, we make each other coffee, so we know how we take our coffee.
Yes. 'How we take our coffee' is how we like it – what we like to put in it.
For example, sugar or milk.
I know that you don't like milk in your coffee.
You take your coffee black.
I do. I like black coffee and you take your coffee white and you used to have sugar, but you don't anymore.
That's right. Occasionally when I'm at home I put some honey in my coffee to make it a bit sweeter.
Eurgh! Honey in coffee? Yes.
Is that surprising? I've never heard of that.
Really? Sugar, but not honey.
But why would that be so bad?
Well, I don't know. It's just I've never heard of it.
It's really good. I would recommend.
OK. So, Georgie, what happens if you don't have your coffee?
Well, in the morning if I don't have coffee, I feel very grumpy and very tired.
In the afternoon if I don't have a coffee, it's not terrible, but I would prefer to have my afternoon coffee.
How about you? Yeah, I need my coffee, especially in the morning, but I don't have my coffee first thing in the morning.
Oh, interesting. I have it, kind of, I don't know...
work time – nine o'clock. Why is that?
I think it's too strong, too powerful.
Or maybe just the way I drink it.
What happens if you drink too much coffee?
Ooh, then it's difficult to sleep because of the caffeine.
Caffeine is that chemical in coffee and tea that makes you feel awake and alert.
But too much means you're too alert.
I don't think that caffeine has a big effect on me.
I don't think I have trouble sleeping if I drink too much coffee.
It's strange. Yeah, because sometimes I'll have an espresso after dinner.
Really? Yeah. And I can still sleep.
That's crazy. Yeah. Lucky me.

title: Talking about lunch
sourceTitle: Talking about lunch: Real Easy English
description: Trưa nay ăn gì? leftovers, skip lunch, hangry (đói + cáu), brunch, working lunch, I'd rather…

segments.text: Hi, Neil. How are you?
I'm hungry. Me too. I'm starving.
Well, that's good, because we're talking about lunch today.
We're recording this just before lunch, so it's no wonder that we're both very hungry.
You might be able to hear our tummies rumble because we're hungry.
OK. So, shall we begin?
Yes. Let's do it. What have you got for lunch today?
Today for my lunch, I have chicken with potatoes and vegetables in a harissa paste.
Oh, that sounds really nice.
Yeah, it's leftovers actually, which I have heated up and brought in, in a little flask.
What are leftovers? Good question.
Leftovers. That's food from a meal that you've already had that you didn't finish and you can heat it up and eat it again.
Yes. I also have leftovers for my lunch today.
So, yesterday I made a pasta for lunch with vegetables in it and I have that.
So, Beth, what do you usually have for lunch?
Is it usually leftovers or something else?
It's usually leftovers when I come into work because it's easier, and then I don't need to buy lunch.
But if I go out and buy food, then I would usually go for something like sushi or ramen.
What about you? What do you usually have for lunch?
Yeah. Sometimes I have leftovers that I bring in.
Sometimes I buy a sandwich, for example.
What's your favourite kind of sandwich?
If I have a sandwich...
if I buy a sandwich for lunch, I like to get things like smoked salmon.
Nice, with pickles maybe. Yeah.
There's a really good baguette I like actually that has smoked salmon and egg mayonnaise in it.
Oh, it's so nice. Stop it.
Sorry. I'm so hungry. Me too.
Neil, do you ever skip lunch?
No. No way! I would be in a horrible mood if I skipped lunch.
I don't understand how anyone can skip any meal.
I need to eat all my meals.
Yeah. Otherwise, you get hangry.
Exactly. 'Hangry' is hungry and angry.
I'm on the... I'm almost getting hangry now.

title: Talking about restaurants
sourceTitle: Talking about restaurants: Real Easy English
description: Bạn có hay đi nhà hàng không? Gọi món, đặt bàn, nhà hàng yêu thích — hội thoại đời thường của Neil và Georgie.

segments.text: Hi, Georgie. How are you?
I'm great, thank you, Neil.
I just had a delicious lunch.
Oh, nice. What did you eat for lunch?
I had pasta. What did you eat?
I had a chicken sandwich.
Mmm. Well, today's episode is all about restaurants and food.
Great. I love it when we talk about food.
Me too. Neil, do you go to restaurants often?
Not that often. Maybe when I meet some friends.
How about you? Do you go to restaurants often?
No, I don't go often.
Probably once a month. OK, and when you go to a restaurant, what's your favourite part of eating there?
I like to be around lots of people.
I really love it when a restaurant has a good atmosphere.
I love spending time with friends.
What about you? Why do you like eating in a restaurant?
Well, I like to go to a restaurant that serves food that I don't know how to cook.
Yep, that's a good point.
So, restaurants with food from countries that I don’t know very well
or that are very different types of food to the food I make.
It’s really nice to eat out and that means to eat not at your home
because you don't have to make the food and you don't have to wash up.
That's true, yes. It’s also nice to eat out for a special occasion.
So, like a birthday or a celebration.
Yes and another special occasion could be something like Christmas and we at BBC Learning English are eating out for that special occasion.
We're having a celebration, aren't we?
Yes, every year we have a Christmas party and we usually eat out in a restaurant.
So, Neil, you said you like eating out in lots of different types of restaurants.
What do you usually order?
Well, I really like spicy food like Indian curries and I like fish.
So I like to get fish curry.
Mmm that sounds delicious! And we have a special way of ordering don't we?
What are some phrases we can use to order things in restaurants?
Yeah, so we can say: 'I'll have the fish curry.'
'I'll have the fish curry, please.'
Yes, and you can also say, 'Can I have the fish curry, please?', as well.

title: Talking about weekend plans
sourceTitle: Talking about weekend plans: Real Easy English
description: Cuối tuần này bạn định làm gì? Cách nói kế hoạch: I'm going to…, I'm planning to…, nothing special.

segments.text: How are you, Neil? I'm well, thank you, Georgie.
How are you? I am pretty good too, thank you.
I'm very excited for the weekend.
Oh, really? Well, today we're talking all about the weekend.
We're going to talk about what we plan to do at the weekend.
Great! Let's start. So, Georgie, do you have any weekend plans?
Yes, I do have plans.
I'm going to visit my parents at the weekend.
So I'm gonna get the train to my home town.
What about you? I don't really have any special plans, but I might spend lots of time doing sport with my kids.
Mm-hm, nice, which sports? Erm, cricket in the summer and football as well.
Nice. So that's what you usually do?
That's what I usually do.
I usually spend most of the weekend taking my kids to sport.
Do you like it? Actually, I really do.
I really do like it.
It's fun to watch them trying their hardest.
Ahh, nice. Is there anything else you'd like to do this weekend?
Well, I might meet up with a friend and we might go for some food
or maybe just a drink or we might go for a walk or something.
Mm, nice! And how about you, Georgie?
What do you plan to do when you get home?
Well, we have a lunch on Saturday.
And we live in the countryside, so we'll probably go for a walk with the dogs
and we're likely to go to the pub as well.
Mm. Is this a typical weekend for you?
It's not because I don't usually go home to see my parents.
Most weekends I stay in London.
I meet some friends. Yeah.
So this is not a typical weekend, but it's nice to visit my parents.
Mm. What are you looking forward to? — This weekend? — Yeah.
I'm really looking forward to spending time in the countryside.
When I'm in London, I really miss the peace and quiet.
And I miss my dog, so I'm looking forward to seeing my dog.
And it's good to get some fresh air.
Yes, exactly, exactly. So, Georgie, you said you are looking forward to being in the countryside.
I did. And 'looking forward to' means that you're 'excited about something you're going to do in the future'.
Exactly, yes. Like I'm looking forward to seeing my dog.
Is your dog looking forward to seeing you?
Yes, I'm sure he is.

title: Talking about public transport
sourceTitle: Talking about public transport: Real Easy English
description: Đi làm bằng gì? Tàu, xe buýt, đi bộ — chuyện trễ tàu, đông người và commute hằng ngày.

segments.text: Hi, Georgie. How are you?
I'm very well, thank you, Neil.
How are you? How was your journey into work?
My journey into work was very good today, actually.
And we're actually talking about transport today.
How was your journey to work?
My journey was quite easy this morning, actually.
It isn't always. And, Neil, we actually have a very similar commute, don't we?
I get the Tube to work, which in the UK is the underground train.
So, I walk to the station around 15 to 20 minutes, and then I get the underground train,
one train, and then I change and then get another one, and then I walk to work.
What about you? I do that, but before, before your bit, I have to get a bus as well.
Are you that far away from the station?
A couple of miles. OK.
Three kilometres. A bit too far to walk, then.
A bit too far to walk.
I have walked when the public transport has been unreliable.
But normally I... I get the bus to the Tube stop, and then I get on the Tube into work.
Lovely. And do you like the Tube?
What do you think about it?
I think the Tube is very convenient, actually, because the trains go very frequently.
So if you miss one, you can wait just a couple of minutes and get the next one.
And it's probably the quickest way to get into central London because there's so much traffic.
Driving is a really bad idea.
Yeah, I agree with you.
It is very reliable. It's usually very easy.
The thing I don't like about it, especially in the morning at rush hour, is the number of people on the Tube.
The... the underground trains in London are very old.
They're very small. And they are very crowded in the mornings.
So 'crowded' means there's lots of people.
We can also say 'packed'.
Yeah, and I really don't like being in a tight space with lots of people in the mornings, so early in the morning.
Yeah, I agree, but I'm lucky because I get on the Tube at the first stop,
so I always get a seat, but then by the time you get on, it is usually really packed.
And the closer you get into central London, the more packed it is.
You're squashed up against strangers.
It's not always fun. I hate it.

title: Talking about routines
sourceTitle: Talking about routines: Real Easy English
description: Một ngày của bạn thế nào? Buổi sáng, đi làm, buổi tối — từ vựng thói quen hằng ngày trong hội thoại thật.

segments.text: How are you today, Neil?
I'm very well, thank you, Beth.
How about you? I'm very good.
So what topic are we talking about in this episode?
OK, well, today's episode is all about habits and routines.
Now we talked about our favourite foods a few weeks ago.
But today we'll talk about our meal times and routines for eating.
Mm, sounds good! What do we mean by a routine, Beth?
Is it different to a habit?
Well, they are similar, but a habit is something we do regularly.
So, for example, I eat an apple and a banana most days. — Ooh, very healthy. — Yeah.
A routine, though, is slightly different.
It's usually more about the time that we do something and the way we do something.
So, I have my breakfast at 6am every day.
OK. You said you have your breakfast at 6am every day.
What do you usually have to eat?
Well, usually I have something simple.
A bowl of cereal, some toast with marmalade.
How about you, Beth? I usually have porridge.
And what about lunch? What time do you have lunch, usually?
Mm, I normally have lunch at about one o'clock.
What about you? Yeah, the same.
I don't like it at 12.
That's too early. But by two, I'm getting a little bit hungry and angry at the same time!
There's a word for that, Neil.
So if you're hungry and angry, we can combine them and say 'hangry'.
Yeah. So it's important to have regular meal times, so you don't get hangry.
That's true. Now you've just reminded me of another word which is 'brunch'.
Now, that's a combination of the words 'breakfast' and 'lunch'.
Do you ever have brunch, Neil?
I love brunch, especially at weekends.
Yeah. When I was at university, I used to have brunch pretty much every day.
So I would meet up with my friends and we would go to a café and we would have brunch.

title: Talking about pets
sourceTitle: Talking about pets: Real Easy English
description: Bạn thích chó hay mèo? Neil và Georgie kể về thú cưng — rất hợp cho Speaking Part 1 chủ đề animals/pets.

segments.text: Hi, Neil. How are things?
Very good, thank you. How are you, Georgie?
Yes, I'm pretty good, thank you, as well.
So, Neil, what are we talking about today?
We are talking about animals.
We'll be talking about pets.
OK, Neil. So do you have any pets?
No, I don't have any pets, but I know you do, Georgie.
Yes, I do. I have a black dog called Rafi. — Rafi? — Yeah.
Did you choose the name?
Partly, but it was a decision we made as a family.
Mm. Did you have pets as a child?
Yes, I did. We used to have cats, actually, we started with cats and then we got a dog and then we also had hamsters.
What about you, Neil? Did you have pets?
No, we didn't have pets when I was young.
Oh, I did have a goldfish called Gilbert.
But then, later on, when I was a teenager, my parents got a cat and a dog. — Wow. — Mm.
Did you have a good relationship with Gilbert?
I don't remember Gilbert, sadly.
But we had a cat that I liked very much and I've never really liked dogs, I'm afraid.
So, Neil, you don't have any pets now and you said you don't like dogs, but will you ever get one?
No, Georgie, I don't think so.
I will never get a dog.
That's OK. I mean, they're not for everyone.
What was your cat like?
The cat made me feel very calm, because she sat on my lap and purred.
You just used the word purr.
Can you explain what that is?
Yeah. 'Purring' is 'the noise that cats make'.
Not miaow. Miaow is... Purring is...
And the cat made that noise and made me feel calm.
Neil, that was a really good purr sound.
I would say it was purr-fect!
So, Georgie, what was your first dog like?
My first dog was really lovely.
I actually used to say that she was my best friend.
And we actually have a common expression to describe dogs, which is man's best friend.
'Man' here means 'human', so human's best friend.
That's because dogs are usually quite loyal.

title: Phrases natives use every day: "Well…"
sourceTitle: Phrases Native Speakers Use Everyday - Part 1
description: "Well…" — từ người bản xứ dùng mỗi ngày để có thời gian suy nghĩ và làm câu trả lời nhẹ nhàng hơn. Ví dụ vui: "Do you like my new dress?"

segments.text: Right, here we go. Number one, well.
Well. We use this for thinking time, but also sometimes to soften an answer.
Imagine the situation. Your wife, you're preparing to go out to a party.
Your wife puts on a new dress.
And she says, "Do you like my new dress?"
And you say, "Well, oh, I need thinking time.
What am I going to say?
Be honest? Be diplomatic? Yeah, it looks great.
And she says, "You don't like it, do you?"
You can't win. I know.
Or you might say, "Well, I'm not sure.
Maybe something more casual for this party?
So, here it's more about softening the answer.

title: Phrases natives use every day: "Actually…"
sourceTitle: Phrases Native Speakers Use Everyday! - Part 2
description: "Actually" để sửa lời người khác ("Actually, I live in Spain") hoặc thêm một sự thật bất ngờ — chú ý ngữ điệu xuống-lên.

segments.text: Number two. Actually. Actually. We use this for correcting people.
But also we use it to maybe add a surprising truth.
Correcting people. Imagine somebody says, "So Keith, you live in England, right?"
Actually, I live in Spain.
I'm correcting them. And often in this case we say actually, falling rising tone.
Actually, I live in Spain.
Okay. Keith, you don't eat fish, right?
Actually, I do eat fish.
Okay. Also adding a surprising truth.
Go back to the situation with my wife and the new dress.
Do you like my new dress?
I actually like it. Great answer cuz it's kind of adding surprise and making them happy, right?
I actually quite like it.
Excellent. It's used I think actually often when you know quite a soft way, informal way to soften things or give a bit of surprise.

title: Phrases natives use every day: "Right…"
sourceTitle: Phrases Native Speakers Use Everyday! - Part 3
description: "Right" rất "British": thể hiện đã hiểu, chuyển sang việc khác ("Right. Let's go.") và ngạc nhiên nhẹ ("Oh, right.").

segments.text: Okay, number three, right. Right.
I like this one. We use this in different situations.
First of all, you can use it to show understanding.
So, when you're listening to your partner explaining something and you go, "Right.
Right. Right." Okay? You're showing understanding, okay?
Another way is we use it for moving on or giving instructions.
There's a bit of a joke that an English man can't stand up until they've said the word right.
So, we say, "Right." And then you stand up and say, "It's time to go.
Right. Let's go. Right. It's time to leave.
Or in in a meeting, everybody's sat down and you go, "Right.
What should we discuss today?
That word at the start, it cracks me up.
It's so British. But it's lovely.
Right. What should we do today?
Also, it can be used for gentle surprise, okay?
Imagine you're going to a party with some friends and then Jack and Mary turn around and say,
"Oh, we're going to get a taxi and you can walk."
Oh, right. Surprise. Oh, right.
I thought we were going together.
"Oh no, sorry. We're in a rush."

title: Late for a meeting — what do you say to your boss?
sourceTitle: What would you say to an angry boss?
description: Đến muộn và sếp hỏi "What time do you call this?" — cách xin lỗi: I got caught in traffic, something urgent came up, this won't happen again.

segments.text: So, imagine you arrive late at a meeting with your boss.
She's not happy and she says, At last, you're here.
What time do you call this?
And then, what would you say?
I'm so sorry I'm late.
I got caught in traffic.
My apologies, the traffic is terrible today.
I'm really sorry, something urgent came up at home.
This won't happen again. And over to you, what would you say?
Let me know in the comments.

title: A friend brings you a gift — what do you say?
sourceTitle: Friend comes round for dinner
description: Bạn đến ăn tối và tặng quà: "Oh, you shouldn't have!", "You needn't have bothered", "That's so kind" — nói cảm ơn tự nhiên như người bản xứ.

segments.text: You've invited a friend round for dinner, and when they arrive, they say, Hey, hi, great to see you.
Oh, and this is for you.
And then what would you say?
You might say, "Oh, that's so kind.
Thanks. Oh, you shouldn't have.
That's lovely. Thanks. Oh, you needn't have bothered.
Thanks. Oh, great, my favorite.
Over to you. What would you say?
Let me know in the comments.

title: Part 1: Home & accommodation — house or flat?
sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 1 - HOME/ACCOMMODATION
description: Chủ đề Accommodation hay gặp ngay đầu bài thi: house or flat, nhà trông thế nào, nhìn ra cửa sổ thấy gì, có định ở lâu không — rented room, three-storey terraced house, airy and spacious, cramped, up in the air.

segments.text: Do you live in a house or a flat?
Currently, I'm living in a rented room in Go Vap District.
It's on the second floor of a three-storey building.
Currently, I'm living in a three-storey terraced house in Phu Nhuan District.
Currently, I'm living on the 20th floor of a block of flats in District 10.
What does it look like?
Oh, it's pretty nice. It's not so big, but it has enough space for me and my roommates to move around comfortably.
However, sometimes when we have guests, it can be a little cramped.
Oh, it's quite airy and spacious. I live with my family and each of us has our own room.
It also has a small garden at the front where I can grow some potted plants and flowers to add some greenery to my house.
Oh, it's fairly spacious but a bit old. My parents bought it many years ago and I've been living there since I was born.
Hopefully, in the future, I can earn more money in order to have it rebuilt, or at least have it redecorated.
What can you see when you look out the window of your room?
Nothing much, to be honest.
I live in a populated area, so all I can see out of my window is just long lines of houses stretching for miles, which is kind of boring to me.
I prefer a view of nature, such as the park view or the ocean view.
Unfortunately, my room doesn't have any windows. Sometimes I wish it had one so that I could enjoy the view out of it.
My room's window overlooks a river, a bridge and many tall buildings, so the view from there is wonderful, especially in the evening when the city lights are lit up.
I think I can look at it all day without getting bored.
Do you plan to live there for a long time?
Well, I'm not sure yet. On the one hand, I love my parents and I want to stay with them so that I can take care of them in case they get sick.
On the other hand, I'd like to move out and live on my own so that I can have more privacy.
My final decision is still up in the air at the moment.
No, not really. I don't really like my current accommodation and I can't picture myself living there for the next one or two years.
As soon as my rental agreement expires, I'll pack my bags and move out right away.
Yeah, I guess so. I love almost everything about my current apartment, so there's no good reason for me to change my accommodation in the not-too-distant future.
I think I'll continue living there for the next four or five years at least.
No, I don't think so. I don't want to live with my parents, so perhaps in the future I'll move to another place to live, especially after I graduate and get a job.

title: Part 1: The area you live in — do you like it?
sourceTitle: THE AREA YOU LIVE IN - Bài mẫu IELTS Speaking Part 1
description: Bạn có thích khu mình sống không, hay đi đâu ở đó? Hai hướng trả lời: close to the city center, an ideal place to reside — hoặc a complicated area, robberies, my rental agreement expires.

segments.text: Do you like the area that you live in?
Yeah, I really enjoy living in my current neighborhood.

I like my bed the most at home. It's soft and comfortable, so I feel good when I lie on it.

Well, the favorite item in my home is definitely my bed.

title: Part 1: Barbecue
sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 1 MODEL ANSWERS - BARBECUE
description: Người Việt có thích đồ nướng không? packed with customers, book a table in advance, makes my mouth water, healthy appetites — mỗi câu hỏi có 2–3 câu trả lời mẫu.

segments.text: Do Vietnamese people like barbecue?
Yeah, I guess so. We have a lot of barbecue places all across the country,
and they are often packed with customers, especially in the evening or on weekends.
Sometimes, if you want to get a table, you even have to book it in advance.
What kind of food do you like to eat for barbecue?
Well, I don't know about other people, but I really love to eat grilled seafood, especially octopuses and shrimps.
They are so tasty to me.
Well, just speaking of it already makes my mouth water.
All types of meat, to be honest, be it pork, beef, or chicken.
I love them all. I don't really have a favorite, because for me, everything tastes better when it's barbecued.
Nothing, to be honest.
Unlike many people out there, I'm not really a big fan of barbecue food.
It usually takes a long time to be well cooked, while I hate to wait when I'm hungry.
Also, it doesn't look so healthy to me.
Would you like to have barbecue with your family or your friends?
I would say I prefer to have it with my friends.
It seems more fun and more comfortable to me.
We can eat as much food as we want, because all of us have healthy appetites.
On top of that, I tend to have more stories to catch up on when I'm with them.
I guess I prefer to have it with my family members.
I can eat as much food as I want without worrying much about money because my parents are usually the ones who pay.
Besides, it's also a great way to spend some quality time with those who I love the most.
Did you have barbecue when you were a child?
No, not pretty often to be honest.
When I was a kid, having a barbecue wasn't as popular as it is now.
Instead of eating food cooked over the fire, I usually went for some hot pot or stir-fry.
I didn't have to wait for a long time to enjoy my food, which was a real blessing to me back then.
Yeah, every now and then.
My mother is a huge fan of barbecue.
So, when I was a little boy, I got to eat grilled food from time to time.
I guess that has unexpectedly aroused my interest in this kind of food.

title: Part 1: New Year — how do you celebrate it?
sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 1 - NEW YEAR
description: Tết của bạn: go back to my parents' home, exchange greetings, cook banh chung, a change of scenery, kill my boredom — và vì sao năm mới là một khởi đầu mới.

segments.text: How do you celebrate New Year?
Well, if you're referring to Vietnamese New Year, I usually go back to my parents' home and spend some quality time with them.
Together, we clean up our house and redecorate it to welcome a new year.
We also pay a visit to our relatives and exchange greetings with each other.
Well, most of the time, I stay home and spend some quality time with my parents.
We usually do a lot of eating and drinking during this time of the year.
Sometimes I also go away, or simply go out with friends for coffee to unwind after a busy year.
Do you still remember a New Year that you celebrated?
Yeah, it was the 2020 celebration.
Due to the recent pandemic, I couldn't go to different places as I did in the previous years.
So it was kind of boring. I spent most of the time staying at home and watching TV to kill my boredom.
Yeah, it was back in 2016. Instead of staying home like we usually do every year, my family decided to spend a few days away for a change of scenery.
We had a wonderful time together and it was a pretty memorable New Year's celebration to me.
Do you have any ceremonies to celebrate a new year in your country?
Yes, my family and I usually get around a big pot to cook banh chung, which is a savory sticky rice cake with mung beans and pork.
It's a really fun and meaningful activity for me because it allows me to have some bonding time with people who mean the most to me.
Why do people think New Year is a new beginning?
Well, I don't know about other countries, but in Vietnam, we have a pretty long holiday to celebrate the New Year.
So it enables us to have plenty of time to reflect on what we have done in the previous year and make plans for a new year to come.
The change in the year number itself also signals a new start.

title: Part 1: Special costumes

description: Hóa trang: Naruto, Goku, Power Rangers, Joker — dress up as, have a whale of a time, I'm not really one for costumes, reduce stress. Mỗi câu hỏi có 2–3 cách trả lời.

segments.text: Do you like to wear special costumes?
Well, not too much now, but when I was a kid, I was really into some cartoon character costumes like Naruto or Goku.
I usually asked my mom to buy this costume for me whenever I saw one.
No, not really, partly because I find these costumes a bit too hard to wear.
Why? I'm the kind of person who gets sweaty quite easily.
With the scorching weather in Ho Chi Minh City, it would be a real nightmare to have them on for many hours.
I guess I prefer watching other people in costume instead of me doing it.
Yeah, I love it an awful lot.
Every year on Halloween, I always have plans to dress up as some of my favorite characters in comic books or in movies.
It's really fun and it's a great way to unwind and reduce stress.
Did you try any special costumes when you were young?
I did. I remember one time when I was at the street market with my mom, I saw a pretty cool Power Rangers costume.
I asked my mom to buy it for me and she did. I can't tell you how happy I was when I put it on.
Just speaking of it brings back so many great memories.
Yeah, a lot, actually. When I was a little girl, my parents usually bought me different special costumes.
They took loads of photos of me in such costumes and then put them in an album.
And every now and then, we take a look back at those photos and have a great time reminiscing about the past.
No, I didn't. Unlike many kids in my neighborhood who were into wearing a special costume to go out, I wasn't really interested in it.
My parents did buy me some costumes back then, but I never put them on.
When was your last time wearing special costumes?
Well, if I'm not mistaken, it was almost 6 years ago.
At the time, I was still a second-year student at university and I took part in a prom night.
I dressed up as Joker, who is my favorite character in DC Comics, and I had a whale of a time that night.
If memory serves, it was almost two years ago. At the time, I took part in a Halloween party at my company and I dressed up as a black witch.
I had a lot of fun that day with my colleagues.
Too bad I couldn't do so last Halloween due to the COVID-19 pandemic.
And with everything going on now, I don't think I can do that again this Halloween either.
As we previously discussed, I'm not really one for costumes, so I can't recall the last time I had one on.
As a matter of fact, I don't think I have ever done that before.
Do you ever buy special costumes?
Yeah, but mostly when I was a little boy. Now I rarely shop for one because I think I'm a little too old for that.
That said, one day when I have kids, I'll definitely buy one for them.
Yeah, almost every year, especially on special occasions like Halloween or Christmas.
I love the idea of dressing up as someone I admire and then trying to be them for a day.
It's such a wonderful way to relax and reduce stress after some tiring days at school.
No, I don't think I ever do so. It's my parents who did that when I was a child.
But as soon as they realized I wasn't really crazy about the whole costume thing, they stopped doing that for good.

title: Part 1: Cooking & baking — Jimmy and Jenny
sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 1 MODEL ANSWERS - COOKING
description: Hội thoại hai người: Jenny mê nấu nướng, Jimmy thì không. culinary skills, my favorite pastime, every once in a while, it does wonders for our health, gravitate towards home-cooked meals.

segments.text: Hey Jenny, did you learn to cook when you were a child?
Yeah, my mom is a really good cook and she taught me how to cook when I was just a little girl.
At first, I didn't expect to enjoy doing it, but it turned out to be really fun and interesting making tasty dishes for other people.
I don't want to brag, but my culinary skills are quite good. How about you, Jimmy?
Well, I must confess that cooking has never been my favorite pastime, so when I was a kid, I didn't care much about it.
My younger sister was really passionate about it and she usually spent time in the kitchen preparing meals with my mother, but I wasn't interested at all.
Okay, second question. Do you often bake?
Yeah, I really love baking. I have an oven at home.
And every once in a while, especially on weekends, I spend around one to two hours baking some desserts for my family.
I usually go online to look for some baking recipes and then try them.
Sometimes it works, sometimes it doesn't, but it brings me a lot of joy. And you?
Well, you may find it hard to believe, but never have I baked anything before.
As I said earlier, I'm not a fan of cooking and I don't have an oven at home either.
Besides, based on my observation, baking is not really a popular cooking technique in Vietnam, especially for home cooking.
The third question. What kind of things are baked in your country?
Well, I guess just like other parts of the world, the Vietnamese usually bake bread or desserts.
Sometimes you may see people bake chicken or pork, but it's kind of uncommon.
For things like meat, fish or vegetables, we prefer using other cooking techniques such as stir-frying, simmering or grilling.
All right, fourth question. Do you think baking is a healthy method of cooking?
Well, as a person who is really passionate about cooking and spends a lot of time reading articles about cooking techniques, I can say that baking is one of the healthiest cooking methods.
Scientifically speaking, it requires little or no added oil, so it does wonders for our health. What do you think?
Well, just to be clear, I'm not a culinary expert, so I'm not quite sure about this.
But I remember reading an article on the internet and it said that baking is considered one of the healthiest ways of cooking. So I think, yeah, it is.
Okay, last question. Do you prefer eating home-cooked meals or eating out?
In fact, I love both of them, but I tend to gravitate towards home-cooked meals.
It is mainly because for me, homemade dishes are usually cheaper, safer and healthier than street foods or even foods in a restaurant.
When you eat at home, you don't need to worry about things like food hygiene or food poisoning.
How about you? Well, I don't cook, so I enjoy going out to eat more.
I can save lots of time on preparing the food or cooking, and I also don't have to do the dishes afterwards, which is a wonderful thing to me.

title: Part 1: Insects — love them or hate them?
sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 1 MODEL ANSWERS - INSECTS
description: Một người mê côn trùng, một người sợ: put me in awe, gives me goosebumps, an abundance of insects, fireflies lighting up the night, pollinate flowers.

segments.text: Okay, first question. How do you like insects?
Believe it or not, I love them an awful lot. In fact, I'm into all creatures on the planet.
I've watched a lot of documentaries about insects and their wonderful features always put me in awe.
And you, Jimmy? Well, I don't like most insects, to be honest.
For me, they are terrible creatures. They look ugly and scary. Some of them are really dirty and smelly.
Just the thought of touching them already gives me goosebumps.
Insects like bees or mosquitoes can sting you and make you hurt or itchy.
Okay, second question. Are there many different insects where you live?
Well, I come from the countryside, so there's an abundance of insects there.
During the day, you can see different species of butterflies flying around, and they're beautifully colorful.
At night, you can hear the buzzing sound of cicadas and watch the fireflies lighting up the night.
And you, Jimmy? Well, I live in Ho Chi Minh, which is a big city, so I don't have a lot of time to see different types of insects.
The most common ones that I encounter are probably mosquitoes or cockroaches because they usually appear in my house.
Sometimes when I go out, I also see some flying insects like dragonflies or butterflies.
All right, last question. Do you think insects are useful?
Yeah, for sure. I believe that every creature plays an important role in our lives and the ecosystem.
For example, bees help pollinate flowers and provide humans with honey.
For other species, at least they can be a part of the food chain. What do you think?
Well, to tell you the truth, I'm not really interested in insects or animals in general, so to my knowledge, I'm not sure if they are useful or not.
The only benefit that I can think of right now is we can make honey from honeybees.

title: Part 1: Farming
sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 1 - FARMING
description: Bạn đã đến nông trại chưa? a cacao farm in Dalat, livestock, the backbone of the economy, born and raised in a rural area, food additives.

segments.text: Have you ever visited a farm?
Yeah, I have. Fortunately, a few years ago, I went on a trip with my family to Dalat and we paid a visit to a cacao farm.
We got a chance to learn about the process of making cocoa and were offered a hot cup of cocoa right on site.
It was a really wonderful experience.
Well, you may find it hard to believe, but I've never been on a farm before.
I've spent my entire life living in the city and I rarely travel to a new place.
So I absolutely have no idea what a farm looks like in reality.
What kind of farm do you like?
I think I prefer a mixed farm where I can see different types of livestock, cattle and crops altogether.
Well, just the thought of it already makes me feel so excited.
Well, as we previously discussed, I've never set foot in any farms before, so it's kind of hard to say which one I like.
But if I were to choose one, it would be a fruit farm, simply because I love fruit and I think it would be great if I could eat some fresh fruit straight from the farm.
What can you do on a farm?
I guess there are plenty of things to do. If you visit a fruit farm, you can water the trees or pick the fruit.
If you are on a livestock farm, you can collect the eggs, milk the cows or simply feed the animals there.
Do you think farming is important?
Yeah, no doubt about that. It provides food and jobs for people all over the world.
Almost everything we eat on a daily basis is related to farming.
For an agriculture-based country where farming is like the backbone of the economy, it's even more important.
Did you do farm work when you were young?
Well, believe it or not, even though I was born and raised in a rural area, I didn't have to do any farm work when I was a child.
It's my mother who had to do it when she was young.
After she gave birth to me, my family no longer had a farm, so I've never had a chance to experience the life of a farmer.
No, not at all. I was born and raised in a big city, so I didn't have to do anything related to farming when I was younger.
It's OK for me, I guess, because I'm not really interested in farm work anyway.
Are there any farms in your hometown?
My hometown has witnessed drastic changes over the past few years, so there are not so many farms left now.
You can still see a few farms there, but most of them are family-run and are quite small.
Yeah, I come from the countryside, so there are loads of farms there.
I remember when I was a kid, sometimes after school, I would go to the green field with my friends to play some traditional outdoor games.
Well, just speaking of it brings back so many great memories.
Do you care much about the process of making food?
Yeah, I really do, especially in this day and age where food chemicals and food additives are widely used.
I have to pay more attention to the things that I put in my mouth.
As a matter of fact, I have seen quite a few videos about the process of making certain kinds of food and they were really fascinating to me.

title: Part 1: Recycling
sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 1 MODEL ANSWERS - RECYCLE
description: Tái chế: got into the habit of recycling, repurpose glass jars, the least of my concern, decompose, raise people's awareness, prevent landfills from getting overloaded.

segments.text: Do you recycle now?
It's kind of embarrassing to say this, but I don't have a habit of recycling things.
Partly because it's not a common routine in Vietnam, and I don't know how to do it.
More often than not, I just put things in a trash bag after I finish using them.
Yeah, I can probably say that I've got into the habit of recycling.
More often than not, I reuse plastic bags for future groceries or as garbage bags.
Sometimes, I also repurpose glass jars and bottles into something useful, like a new container for other household items or a planter for my flowers.
Did you recycle when you were a kid?
No, I almost never did.
When I was a kid, all I could think of was doing my homework and then going out to play some traditional outdoor games with my childhood friends.
The thought of reusing things was the least of my concern back then.
Yeah, believe it or not, I did. My parents taught me to recycle things from a very young age.
So, unlike other kids in my neighborhood who never seemed to care about it, I always try to come up with ways to reuse recyclable items for my own home use.
Will you recycle in the future?
Yeah, I think I will. Environmental pollution is a big thing now, so I'll be willing to change my routine for the sake of the environment.
I guess I'll start by doing some research on the internet on how to recycle things effectively.
Can you name products and materials that are commonly recycled?
I guess, just like other parts of the world, Vietnamese people usually have things made of plastic and glass material recycled,
mainly because these materials may take thousands of years to decompose in the environment.
Batteries are also a common type of products in this category.
Why have people's attitudes towards recycling changed over the last several years?
In my opinion, one of the main reasons is that environmental pollution is a pressing problem nowadays.
And the press and the media have been talking a lot about this topic over the past few years.
So it has helped raise people's awareness of recycling in general.
Do you think recycling is important?
Yeah, no doubt about that. If everyone can develop a habit of recycling, it will help reduce the amount of waste produced
and prevent landfills from getting extremely overloaded, which in turn makes the environment become cleaner.

title: Part 1: Study — what is your major?
sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 1 MODEL ANSWERS - STUDY
description: Dành cho sinh viên: I'm majoring in…, writing and cracking codes, I must confess, without thinking twice, has never crossed my mind, go back to square one.

segments.text: What is your major?
I'm majoring in business administration.
Most of the time, I study about different aspects of a business like accounting, marketing or human resources.
It's hard work, but I find it pretty intriguing.
I'm an IT major and I spend most of my time sitting in front of the screen writing and cracking codes.
It's a difficult major and it can be pretty stressful at times.
Why did you choose to study that major?
I must confess, when I was a high school student, I didn't know what I wanted to do with my life.
So I asked my parents for advice and they told me to choose this major.
From a very young age, I already knew that I was gonna be a doctor when I grew up.
I have always wanted to help improve everyone's health or even save their lives.
That's why I went for this major without thinking twice.
Would you like to change your major if you got the chance?
No, definitely not. I really enjoy what I've been studying, so the thought of switching to another major has never crossed my mind.
Yeah, I think I would. I find my current major pretty dull and boring,
so it would be great if I could switch to another one, even though it means I have to go back to square one and start over.

title: Fun, funny or happy?
sourceTitle: Fun, funny và happy, đều là sự khác nhau?
description: Tiểu phẩm vui: "I feel so funny when I'm with him" — sai rồi! Phân biệt fun (vui, dễ chịu), funny (buồn cười) và happy. Còn "I feel funny" lại nghĩa là thấy hơi ốm.

segments.text: Hey, what do you think of Jimmy?
He's a very fun guy. He usually tells jokes and makes me laugh. I feel so funny when I'm with him.
I see. I think what you really meant was he's a funny guy and you feel happy when you're with him.
Huh? Oh yeah. So what's the difference between them?
Hmm, that's simple. You use the word "funny" to describe a person who usually tells jokes and makes you laugh.
You use the word "fun" to describe a person who you enjoy being with.
For example, Jimmy is a fun guy to be with because he knows many interesting stories.
When it comes to feelings, you don't use either the word "funny" or "fun", but instead you use the word "happy".
"I feel happy staying at home all day."
If you say you feel funny, it means that you're slightly ill or sick.
And that's enough for today's video. Follow for more.

title: Coffee? Not for my handsome face! (Band 5 → 8)
sourceTitle: Do you often drink coffee? Band 5-6-7-8 samples
description: Câu hỏi Part 1 "Do you often drink coffee?" trả lời 4 mức band với lý do… bảo vệ khuôn mặt đẹp trai: allergic to caffeine, jittery, break out, a nightmare.

segments.text: Do you often drink coffee?
No, I rarely drink coffee. I feel uncomfortable when I drink it.
It can make my skin look bad and affect my handsome face.
No, I rarely drink coffee because it makes my stomach uncomfortable. If I drink it, I'll have to go to the toilet right away.
On top of that, it's not good for my skin because it can make acne appear on my handsome face.
No, I almost never drink coffee as I'm allergic to caffeine.
Whenever I have a sip, my stomach feels uneasy and I have to rush to the bathroom, which is terrible.
Besides, drinking coffee can cause acne on my handsome face, and I definitely don't want that.
No, absolutely not. Coffee is the last thing I'd ever want to drink, to be honest. Mainly because I'm allergic to caffeine.
Even just a small sip makes me feel jittery and sends me rushing to the bathroom, which is honestly a nightmare.
On top of that, it makes me break out and I really don't want anything messing up my handsome face.

title: Remembering names — only the pretty ones? (Band 5 → 8)
sourceTitle: Can you remember people's names? Band 5-6-7-8
description: Nhớ tên con gái thì nhanh, tên con trai thì quên ngay — "maybe my brain is just biased". Luyện it depends, when it comes to…, it's a different story.

segments.text: Can you remember people's names?
It depends. I can remember girls' names really fast, but I can't remember boys' names.
It depends. I can remember girls' names really quickly, especially if they're pretty,
but when it comes to boys' names, I usually struggle a lot. I don't know why.
Well, I think it depends. I can remember girls' names really quickly, especially if they're pretty.
But when it comes to boys' names, I always struggle. I tend to forget them right away. I have no idea why.
Well, it sort of depends on the situation.
When it comes to girls, especially the pretty ones, I can remember their names really quickly, but it's a different story with boys' names.
For some reason, I always struggle to remember them and often forget almost instantly. Maybe my brain is just biased.

title: Time management: eight dates in one day (Band 5 → 8)
sourceTitle: Are you good at time management? Band 5-6-7-8
description: Khoe kỹ năng quản lý thời gian bằng một ví dụ "khó đỡ": hẹn hò 8 cô gái trong một ngày! plan ahead, get my priorities in order, I wouldn't be exaggerating if…

segments.text: Are you good at time management?
Yes, I'm good at time management. I can manage my time to go out with eight girls a day and to have time for myself.
Yeah, I think my time management skills are quite good because I always plan things carefully.
You know what? I can make time to go out with eight girls in a day and still have time for myself if I want.
Yeah, as an organized person, I believe I excel at managing time. I always plan ahead and know how to get my priorities in order.
A good example is that I once made time to go out with eight different girls in a single day and still had time for myself.
Yeah, I wouldn't be exaggerating if I said I'm a master at managing time.
I always plan ahead by making a daily to-do list and setting my priorities straight the night before.
Believe it or not, I once managed to go out with eight different girls in a single day and still had time for myself.

title: Smombie — the smartphone zombie
sourceTitle: Smombie: The English We Speak
description: Feifei mải nhìn điện thoại nên… đâm sầm vào cửa. "Smombie" = smartphone + zombie: người cắm mặt vào điện thoại khi đi đường, chẳng để ý gì xung quanh.

segments.text: Hello and welcome to The English We Speak.
I'm Neil and joining me today is…
Argh! Ouch!
…Feifei… who's just walked right into a door.
Hi. I was just catching up on some messages on my phone and I sort of lost track of where I was.
Hmm yes, you were walking around like a zombie – a smartphone zombie.
A smombie is a person who walks around with their head bowed down,
writing messages or playing games on their phone and not paying any attention to the world around them!
Even if they're in a situation which might be dangerous – like crossing a road.
Or walking into a radio studio door!
How's your nose?
OK, OK, Neil.
You've made your point.
Let's hear some examples.
I'm too terrified to drive past the college these days.
You never know when a smombie's going to step out into the road in front of the car!
I was knocked flying the other day by a smombie as I was trying to get a bus.
I don't even think she knew she'd bumped into me!
People don't know how to communicate with each other face-to-face any more.
They are such smombies!
This is The English We Speak from BBC Learning English and in this programme we're learning a really new word
which is made up of two words – smartphone and zombie.
The word is smombie.
It's actually from German and has won Germany's 'Youth Word of the Year' competition.
But people are now starting to use it in English too.
It describes people who walk around totally absorbed by their smartphones.
You know, the kind of people who walk into the road without looking at the traffic… Or into studio doors.
Enough now Neil!
Goodbye! Bye.

title: Digital detox
sourceTitle: Digital detox: The English We Speak
description: Neil mất ngủ, mỏi mắt, đau cổ… "Bác sĩ" Feifei kê đơn: a digital detox — một thời gian tránh xa mọi thiết bị có Internet. Và chiếc điện thoại của Neil thì…

segments.text: Hello and welcome to The English We Speak. I'm Feifei.
And I'm Neil.
Ooo. You don't sound too good, Neil.
What's up? Are you sick?
I feel sick.
What are the symptoms?
OK, Dr Feifei.
Here we go: I can't sleep, I feel anxious all the time,
I can't concentrate on anything, I have itchy eyes, I'm tired, my neck hurts...
I've terrible headaches.
Ah, I know what the problem is.
Do you happen to spend a lot of time online?
Yes - all the time.
Do you keep your phone with you in bed, at dinner, in the toilet?
Yes, yes, yes, of course - what's this got to do with how awful I feel?
You need a detox.
A detox? But I haven't drunk any alcohol for months, I exercise every day and I only eat organic food.
No - you need a digital detox.
A digital detox is a period of time away from all devices that can connect to the internet.
I can't do that!
It's impossible! It'll get even worse!
What if someone likes my status at 4am and I miss it!?
Now that IS a sign you're addicted.
You really do need a digital detox.
Let's hear some examples.
My phone broke the day I went on holiday which forced me to have a digital detox.
I felt so relaxed.
I spend all day and night on Saturdays on social media so I need a digital detox every Sunday
or I'm too tired to go to work on Monday.
Right. Here's the key to the safe I've locked all my gadgets in.
I'm going to do this digital detox even if it kills me!
This is The English We Speak from BBC Learning English.
And I'm with Neil, who uses his smartphone, tablet and laptop so much, he's made himself ill.
And Dr Feifei here has prescribed a strict digital detox.
We use the word 'detox' more generally to describe a period when you stop doing something harmful - like drinking too much alcohol or eating junk food.
And so a digital detox is a break from all electronic gadgets.
OK, well here's my phone, Feifei.
I'll deal with that.
Oh no! I suppose it's for the best. Goodbye.
Dr Feifei always knows best.

title: Whizz-kid
sourceTitle: Whizz-kid: The English We Speak
description: Rob mơ làm "thần đồng tài chính" — a whizz-kid: người trẻ, giỏi và thành công. Nhưng Feifei nhắc Rob không còn trẻ… có lẽ anh chỉ hợp ngồi sofa xem TV.

segments.text: Hello and welcome to The English We Speak. I'm Feifei.
And I'm Rob.
Hey Rob, have you ever wondered what you'd be doing if you weren't here?
Hmmm... Lying on the sofa, watching TV I expect.
No Rob. I mean in your career - if you weren't a talented presenter like you are?
I'd be a financial whizz-kid: investing in the stock market, making loads of money.
A whizz-kid? You mean someone young, very clever and successful at doing something?
Yes, that's a whizz-kid!
I don't know why I didn't do it.
Do you want me to tell you?
No. Let's just hear about some other whizz-kids who are young, intelligent and successful, just like me...
My nephew is a computer whizz-kid: he earns a fortune fixing people's laptops!
Our new financial whizz-kid has come straight from university and he's doing really well.
She was a whizz-kid at university, so it's no wonder she's now a partner at one of the top legal firms.
So they are whizz-kids - clever, successful or skilful people - and most of all, they are young, like kids!
And there's the problem Rob.
A problem?
Yes, you're not young anymore.
OK, clever then!
Hmm, I'm not so sure about that.
Alright, successful - one out of three isn't bad.
Well, erm, errr...
OK. Perhaps I'd never be a financial whizz-kid.
Maybe I'll stick to my other plan.
Which is?
Sitting on the sofa, watching TV.
I'm off to do it now. Bye.
Hmm, not a whizz-kid then, just a lazy man. Bye.

title: GOAT — the greatest of all time
sourceTitle: GOAT - The English We Speak
description: Feifei bị gọi là "a goat" (con dê) nên rất bực — hóa ra GOAT = Greatest Of All Time. Feifei và Roy tranh nhau xem ai mới là GOAT!

segments.text: Hello and welcome to The English We Speak.
I'm Feifei. And I'm Roy!
I'm glad you're here, Feifei.
I'm really upset!
Rob just sent me an email saying 'thanks for all my hard work and that I was a goat!'
I think that email was intended for me - for I am the GOAT.
It makes me very happy when people call me that!
You like being called a goat?
No, Roy. GOAT is an acronym for the 'Greatest Of All Time'.
That's why that email was meant for me.
Ahhh that makes more sense about why Rob would call me a GOAT, because I did bake him over a thousand biscuits.
Well, I'll buy him 2000 biscuits from the shop and then we'll see who Rob thinks is the GOAT.
Clearly everyone thinks it's me.
You're very competitive, Feifei!
Plus, I baked, not bought the biscuits.
Let's calm down while we listen to some examples.
That footballer is truly amazing.
Every ball she touches ends in a goal.
She's the GOAT!
Have you seen the new film in the Pelican series?
The special effects, story and acting are all perfect.
It's the GOAT.
My friend said that Ed Sheeran is the GOAT, but I'm not sure I agree.
He's not my favourite artist.
This is The English We Speak from BBC Learning English, and we're talking about the expression 'GOAT'.
'GOAT' is short for 'greatest of all time' and is used to talk about things or people that we think are the best.
Yes, for example footballers or other sports stars who you think are number 1.
You can call them the GOAT.
It can be a way to express your opinion.
You can even use it for video games or films.
For example, the film that I think is the GOAT is ...
Don't even finish that sentence, Roy!
No film that you like could be considered good - let alone the GOAT.
Right - well, at least Rob thinks that I'm the GOAT.
I'll go and say thanks to him for his kind email!
OK Roy, bye! Bye!

title: It beats me!
sourceTitle: How to say it beats me - The English We Speak
description: Rob nói "beats me" và… bị Feifei gõ bằng gậy! "It beats me" = tôi chịu, không hiểu nổi. Vậy ai là thủ phạm khiến văn phòng có chuột?

segments.text: Hello and welcome to The English We Speak.
I'm Feifei and hello, I'm Rob.
Hey Rob, do you know what's going on in the office today?
The boss has been shouting, Helen's crying and Neil doesn't look very happy either.
Beats me. Ouch.
What did you do that for?
You said 'beat me'.
No, no. I mean it beats me.
Ouch! You are strange Rob.
No Feifei. I said 'it beats me' to mean I don't know or I don't understand something.
I knew that Rob I just liked hitting you with this stick!
Very funny. Shall we hear some examples?
It beats me how Stephanie ever got that promotion.
Can you believe that Dave and Andrea are still married!
He's always bossing her around.
It beats me why she stays with him.
It beats me how Jen can afford a new sports car when she only works part-time.
So that is 'it beats me' - a phrase used for saying that you do not know or understand something.
So there's no beating involved!
Definitely not. So now I can safely say, it beats me what's going on in the office - I haven't got a clue.
Well the situation seemed very tense and the boss was shouting something about mice.
Mice? Ah yes, well in that case, it could be that I left my lunch on my desk overnight
and it's possible the mice have found it and eaten it.
They do get everywhere.
Mice! In our office?
I hate mice.
Ouch! Why are you beating me again?
I think it's time to go. Bye. Bye.

title: Have a pop
sourceTitle: Have a pop: The English We Speak
description: Rob "have a pop" (thử) sửa máy tính cho Feifei — và xóa mất kịch bản. "Have a pop at someone" còn có nghĩa là chỉ trích, thậm chí đánh ai đó!

segments.text: Hello and welcome to The English We Speak. I'm Feifei...
...and hello, I'm Rob.
Rob, I'm having a bit of trouble with my computer...
What, again! What's the problem this time?
Well, I've written the script for this programme, but it won't save.
And I can't print it out - this computer just does not work.
Can you fix it?
Let me have a pop at it.
A pop? Are you going to make it explode?
That's a bit extreme, Rob.
Don't worry, Feifei.
If I have a pop at something, I just mean I'll try and do it -
so I'll have a go at doing something, like fixing your computer...
Right! OK, Rob, have a pop then.
But just don't delete all my work.
Don't worry, Feifei, I would never do that, would I?
Let's hear some more examples of the phrase while I sort this out...
I'm going to have a pop at doing this online application for a passport - apparently it's really easy.
We had a pop at making a cake but we baked it for too long and it burnt!
Why not have a pop at yoga?
I've heard it's good for your mind, body and soul.
This is The English We Speak from BBC Learning English and we're talking about the phrase 'have a pop', which means to try something.
So, Rob, you've had a pop at fixing my computer... any luck?
Ermm, not exactly.
Everything seems to have disappeared from the screen.
Let me look...
No! You have deleted my script.
Hmm, Rob, did you know that 'have a pop' has another meaning?
Oh yeah, what's that?
To 'have a pop' also means to criticise or even to try and hit someone.
And I'm going to have a pop at you for losing my script.
Hold... hold on, Feifei.
If we don't have a script, we won't know what will happen next.
I think the listeners know, Rob, don't they? Bye.
Bye. Ouch!

sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 + 3: Describe an important old thing that your family has kept for a long time
title: Part 2: An important old thing your family has kept
description: Album ảnh gia đình — "báu vật" truyền qua ba thế hệ: an heirloom, passed down, vague memories, flip through the album, reminisce about meaningful milestones, learn about their roots.

segments.text: Describe an important old thing that your family has kept for a long time.
Well, I'd like to talk about my family photo album,
which is actually a really meaningful heirloom that has been passed down for at least three generations.
As the name suggests, it's basically a collection of photographs of my family members, and they come in all kinds of shapes and sizes.
Some are just old black and white pictures with pretty poor image quality because, you know, they were taken decades ago.
I think the first time I came across this album was about, let's see, 5 years ago on my grandfather's death anniversary.
My aunts and uncles had all gathered at my house and after we finished the meal, my mother brought out the album.
We sat together and slowly went through every single photo.
That moment really stuck with me because, you know, I got to hear so many fascinating stories about the past,
about people who were young, old, still alive, or even long gone.
Before that day, I only had vague memories of my childhood
and absolutely no idea what my parents or relatives looked like when they were younger.
So flipping through the album was honestly quite exciting for me.
I guess the main reason why this album is incredibly important to my family is that it gathers all our special moments in one place.
So in the future we can look back and reminisce about meaningful milestones.
Also, it's a way for the younger generations to learn about their roots just like it helped me learn about mine.

sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 + 3: Describe an important old thing that your family has kept for a long time
title: Part 3: Why do people keep old things?
description: Vì sao người ta giữ đồ cũ? emotional value, hold on to, sturdy wooden furniture, mementos, sentimentally valuable — và giới trẻ ngày nay lưu kỷ niệm trên điện thoại.

segments.text: What kind of old things do people like to keep?
I'm not completely sure, but from what I've observed, people usually keep old things that have a strong emotional value.
They hold on to items that are tied to special memories, like family photos and written letters or gifts from loved ones.
These things help them relive meaningful moments from the past, so they're really hard to throw away.
Also, another category would be durable household items, especially wooden furniture.
You know, in Vietnam, a lot of middle-aged people keep things like solid wood tables,
cabinets, or chairs for decades because they're sturdy and quite valuable.
Why do people keep old things?
Well, I think one of the main reasons is that people usually develop a strong emotional attachment to certain old items.
These objects serve as mementos of the beautiful moments or important milestone they have been through.
So when they look at them, they can reminisce about their past and feel connected to those memories again.
Also, many people keep old things simply because they are still useful or high quality.
For example, older furniture or tools are often sturdier than modern ones.
So, people feel it's wasteful to throw them away.
What's the difference between things people keep now and in the past?
To be honest, I don't think there's a huge difference.
People today still keep things that are sentimentally valuable or financially worth keeping.
I guess the only real change is that younger generations prefer storing their memories digitally and place more importance on convenience and practicality.
I mean instead of using photo albums, they save like thousands of pictures and videos on their phones.
And rather than holding on to bulky furniture or old souvenirs, they tend to choose items that are compact, stylish, and easy to use.

sourceTitle: IELTS PART 2 + 3: Describe a time when someone you know found a clever solution to a problem
title: Part 2: Someone who found a clever solution to a problem
description: Anh trai dùng AI làm "ảnh siêu âm có giun" để con bỏ ăn vặt — vừa buồn cười vừa thông minh: came up with a brilliant way, freaked out, worked like a charm.

segments.text: Describe a time when someone you know found a clever solution to a problem.
I'd like to tell you how my older brother came up with a brilliant way to stop his son from eating too much junk food.
Actually, I didn't witness it in person, but I saw it in a video he posted on social media.
It happened quite recently. Around 2 months ago.
At the time, his son had developed a habit of eating unhealthy snacks on a daily basis.
No matter how hard his parents tried to talk him out of it, he kept asking for them.
My brother then came across an idea online and decided to give it a try.
First, he used an AI tool to create what looked like an ultrasound scan of a stomach with some,
you know, creepy-looking worms moving around inside it.
He then pretended to be a doctor and performed an ultrasound scan on his son's belly.
When his son saw the footage, he completely freaked out and started crying.
From that moment on, he promised to try his best to stay away from unhealthy snacks.
It was quite hilarious, but clever at the same time.
To tell you the truth, I'd never imagined that someone could use AI for something like that.
I called my brother afterwards and asked him whether it had actually worked.
And believe it or not, it had.
The whole thing actually reminded me of my own childhood.
You know, my parents used to tell me that something nasty might grow inside my stomach if I ate too much junk food.
Even though it scared me at the time, it did help me stay away from unhealthy snacks.
So, based on my experience, I could understand why my brother tried this method.
It might not work for every child, but in his son's case, it worked like a charm,
which is why I thought it was such a clever solution.

sourceTitle: IELTS PART 2 + 3: Describe a time when someone you know found a clever solution to a problem
title: Part 3: Are children born clever?
description: Trẻ sinh ra đã thông minh hay học mà thành? genius aside, mentally stimulating activities, well-rounded, an oversupply of workers, physical attributes, at the end of the day.

segments.text: Do you think children are born clever, or do they learn to be clever?
Mhm, that's an interesting one, I must say.
I think it can be both.
Genius aside, some children may be naturally more intelligent than their peers, partly because of genetics.
Others may not be so bright at first,
but they can develop their intelligence over time by doing mentally stimulating activities like reading, studying, or solving puzzles.
Then, there are also kids who are born smart and work hard to become even better.
How important are schools in helping children become more clever?
I'd say schools play a crucial role in that.
You know, schools provide an environment where children can, like, discover their strengths and weaknesses with their teacher's support.
They can get a clearer picture of what they're good at and where they need to improve,
which can help them develop in a more well-rounded way.
That said, the role of parents is just as important, since nobody understands a child better than their mom and dad.
Do you agree or disagree that very clever children are usually happy?
I partly agree with this idea.
It's true that smart kids tend to have an easier time academically, since they can learn much faster than others.
They may also receive a lot of praise and admiration from people around them,
but that doesn't necessarily mean that they're happier than those who aren't as clever.
For me personally, the way they're raised, the environment they grow up in,
and the experiences they have growing up play a much bigger role in their levels of happiness.
Why may a person be very good at one thing, but not another?
Oh, I guess that's perfectly normal, because as far as I know, to become excellent at something,
you need to spend a huge amount of time practicing and learning, potentially thousands of hours.
That's why it's extremely hard for one person to master many different things.
Of course, there are some people who excel in multiple fields, but they're only a small minority.
Why does society need people with different types of intelligence?
Well, I'm not an expert on intelligence, but I suppose it probably comes down to variety.
I mean, if society only had people with one type of intelligence,
there would be an oversupply of workers in one field and a shortage in others.
And that definitely wouldn't be ideal for a sustainable economy.
For example, if everyone were a doctor, then who would be the engineers, entertainers, or teachers?
Do you think people can become very good at anything if they try hard enough?
Mhm, I wouldn't say so.
I don't deny that with enough effort and practice, you can become like reasonably good at almost anything.
But it takes more than just hard work to achieve greatness.
You will also need a bit of talent, and in some cases, certain physical attributes.
For example, in professional sports, factors like height, body type, or natural athletic ability can give some people a significant advantage.
And these aren't things that you can completely change through hard work.
At the end of the day, it really depends on what you are trying to become good at.

sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 + 3: Describe an environmental protection law that you would like to introduce
title: Part 2: An environmental protection law you would like to introduce
description: Luật môi trường bạn muốn đưa ra: phạt nặng xả rác nơi công cộng như Singapore — stricter regulations, heavy fines, think twice, notoriously strict, work hand in hand.

segments.text: Describe an environmental protection law that you would like to introduce.
I've got to be honest with you.
This is the last topic that I want to see in this test since I'm by no means interested in laws in general.
That said, I do sometimes read news or watch videos about pollution.
So, if I were to introduce a new law related to environmental protection in Vietnam,
I would probably bring in stricter regulations on littering in public places.
You know, at the moment, many local people still have a bad habit of throwing different types of waste on the streets
or into lakes and rivers for convenience without paying attention to how much harm this could cause to the environment.
The situation is even worse at tourist attractions or on beaches.
As a result, it's quite common to see plastic bags, takeaway cups, and food containers,
and things like that piled up in one place or scattered around the streets.
The worst thing is that this plastic waste can take hundreds of years to break down even when it ends up in landfills.
That's why a law to stop this is extremely crucial.
Violators would have to pay heavy fines, so they would think twice before acting.
As far as I know, this issue has been going on for a while,
and even though the government has warned people not to litter on different social media platforms, the situation hasn't improved much.
So, stricter enforcement could help.
I actually got this idea partly from Singapore, where the penalties for littering are notoriously strict.
It wouldn't be as clean as it is now if the penalties weren't so severe.
Hopefully, the government and local authorities will work hand in hand to deal with this problem,
and a new law like this will be introduced soon so that the country can become cleaner again.

sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 + 3: Describe an environmental protection law that you would like to introduce
title: Part 3: Protecting the environment: laws, schools & governments
description: Sáu câu hỏi về bảo vệ môi trường: pressing issues, harmful emissions, take greater responsibility, raise awareness, the brink of extinction, no ifs, ands, or buts.

segments.text: Why is environmental protection important?
I guess one obvious reason is that environmental degradation has become one of the most pressing issues these days.
We hear an awful lot about things like air and water pollution, climate change, and global warming,
and these problems can have a direct impact on our health and overall quality of life.
The problem is that the situation has been getting worse over the past few decades.
So, if we don't take action now, we could end up facing pretty serious consequences in the long run.
What environmental problems are common in cities?
Well, in my view, there are plenty of environmental problems in urban areas nowadays, but air pollution is probably among the most serious ones.
This is mainly because large cities are usually packed with vehicles and have a large number of factories,
both of which release huge amounts of harmful emissions every day.
This can seriously worsen air quality and potentially affect people's health in the long run.
And air pollution isn't the only issue.
You know, things like noise pollution, water pollution, and poor waste management are also fairly common in big cities.
Should governments or individuals take more responsibility?
I think both sides have a role to play, but governments probably need to take greater responsibility because,
you know, they have a lot more power and resources to bring about large-scale change.
For example, they can introduce environmental regulations, invest in public transport and renewable energy, and penalize companies that cause excessive pollution.
That said, individuals do need to do their part by using less plastic, recycling, or making more sustainable choices in their everyday lives.
So, I'd say governments should lead the way,
but citizens should also contribute to these efforts rather than leaving governments to deal with everything on their own.
How can schools teach children about environmental protection?
Wow, that's a big question, but from my perspective, schools can start by raising students' awareness of the need to protect the environment.
One way to do this is by integrating environmental lessons into the curriculum,
so children can understand why environmental protection matters and what kinds of human activities can cause harm.
Another possible approach is to organize field trips or outdoor activities that allow students to,
like, connect with nature and learn about environmental issues firsthand.
I think once children develop a stronger connection with the natural world, they're much more likely to take action to protect it.
Do you think environmental laws are effective?
Yeah, I suppose so, at least to some extent.
Otherwise, governments probably wouldn't rely on them so heavily to deal with environmental problems.
Take hunting and poaching, for example.
In the past, before stricter laws were introduced,
many wild animals were killed and some species were even pushed to the brink of extinction because of these activities.
However, stricter regulations have helped protect endangered species and reduce illegal hunting,
which speaks volumes about the role of environmental laws in protecting the environment.
Should companies be punished for pollution?
Yes, beyond a shadow of a doubt.
You know, pollution is a serious issue these days and it can affect people on a large scale.
So, in my view, not just companies, but also individuals who cause serious pollution should be punished.
No ifs, ands, or buts.
In fact, I'd go as far as to say that the stricter the punishment is,
the better because the penalties need to be strong enough to stop both companies and individuals from putting profit or convenience before the environment.

sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 + 3: Describe a piece of advertisement with a famous person in it
title: Part 2: An advertisement with a famous person in it
description: Quảng cáo dầu gội Clear Men có Cristiano Ronaldo: a commercial break, anti-dandruff, a huge fan base, grab people's attention, rush out and buy.

segments.text: Describe a piece of advertisement with a famous person in it.
I've got to be honest with you.
I was a bit freaked out when I read this topic because I rarely watch ads that feature celebrities these days.
Most of the time, I just watch ads on social media from online content creators that I follow.
That said, I do remember a TV commercial that I came across like a while ago when I was watching a TV show with my mom back in my hometown.
And this commercial came on during a commercial break.
It was advertising Clear Men, you know, a popular anti-dandruff shampoo.
In terms of content, there wasn't anything particularly special about it.
It was basically about a man using Clear Men shampoo and becoming free of dandruff afterwards.
