So, he recommended the product to others.
A pretty typical shampoo advertisement.
However, what made this ad stick with me, and probably with many other viewers as well,
was the fact that the man in the ad was Cristiano Ronaldo, one of the greatest footballers in the world.
He has a huge fan base all over the world and I'm one of his fans.
So, having him in the commercial obviously made it more appealing, especially to football fans.
The ad itself wasn't very long.
I guess it was only about 30 seconds, but just seeing Ronaldo in the ad was enough to grab people's attention.
When I was younger, I probably would have bought the product as a way to support him,
but now that I'm a bit older, I've become much more selective about the products I choose to buy.
So, even though I enjoyed seeing Ronaldo in the commercial, it didn't make me want to rush out and buy the shampoo.
So, yeah, I think that's pretty much it.

sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 + 3: Describe a piece of advertisement with a famous person in it
title: Part 3: Why do companies use celebrities in adverts?
description: Vì sao quảng cáo dùng người nổi tiếng? A-list celebrities, a paid promotion, bombarded with ads, get the message across, a false sense of need, impressionable.

segments.text: Why do companies use celebrities in advertisements?
I'd say it's mainly because it's a really effective way to advertise a product.
I mean, famous people, especially A-list celebrities, usually have a huge fan base.
And when their fans see them recommending something, they're more likely to buy it, even if they know it's a paid promotion.
After all, companies wouldn't keep using celebrity endorsements if they didn't work, right?
Are advertisements more creative nowadays?
Oh, yeah, no doubt about that, especially those on social media.
You know, as someone who spends quite a lot of time scrolling through different online platforms,
I can say that many ads these days are so creative that sometimes you don't even realize you're watching an ad until you're halfway through it or even near the end.
In fact, thanks to some young content creators,
I've actually become more willing to sit through ads instead of automatically skipping them like I used to.
What makes an advertisement effective?
Well, I'm not an expert on advertising, but from a viewer's perspective, I'd say one of the most important factors is creativity.
You know, nowadays, people are often bombarded with ads every single day.
So, if advertisers cannot come up with an original way to get the message across, I suppose it'll be difficult to grab people's attention.
Another key factor is how clear and concise the ad is.
If it's short, straight to the point, and presents the key information in a visually engaging way,
it's more likely to appeal to its target audience.
Do children get influenced by advertisements easily?
Yeah, especially when it comes to things they're particularly interested in, like toys or sweets.
You know, generally speaking, ads are often designed in a way that creates a false sense of need
while children, especially younger ones, are still very impressionable.
They're more likely to be drawn to what they see in ads and then ask their parents to buy it for them.
That's why I think parents should keep an eye on the kinds of ads their children are exposed to.

sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 + 3 Band 8 Samples: Describe a person who is good at learning languages
title: Part 2: A person who is good at learning languages
description: Người giỏi ngoại ngữ — thầy Jimmy, một "polyglot": put what I learned into practice, pick up natural expressions, living proof, push myself harder.

segments.text: Describe a person who is good at learning languages.
Well, this immediately reminds me of my English teacher, Jimmy, who I describe as a real polyglot.
I think I first came across him about a year ago when I was looking for an online English course
and happened to find one of his videos.
I was particularly impressed by how fluent and natural his English sounded.
So, I decided to sign up for one of his courses.
At first, I assumed English was the only foreign language he was really good at,
but later I found out that he could also speak Chinese and Korean, as well as a little Indonesian.
I was honestly quite surprised and I remember thinking, "How did he manage to find the time to learn all of them?"
I once asked him for some advice and he told me to take every opportunity to put what I learned into practice.
He also emphasized that I shouldn't be afraid of making mistakes because they're a normal part of the learning process.
On top of that, he suggested watching TV series about everyday life
because they could help me pick up natural expressions instead of learning English only from textbooks.
You know, he's been using these methods for years.
So, in a way, he's living proof that they work.
Needless to say, I really admire him and he's usually the first person I turn to whenever I need advice on language learning.
In fact, he's inspired me to push myself harder every day and is one of the reasons I'm sitting here taking the test today.
I know I still have a long way to go before I reach his level,
but with his guidance and my own determination, I believe I can become a much better language learner in the future.

sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 + 3 Band 8 Samples: Describe a person who is good at learning languages
title: Part 3: Learning foreign languages
description: Học ngoại ngữ: vì sao có người giỏi hơn, trẻ em có học nhanh hơn không, cách học tốt nhất ("no one-size-fits-all method"), công nghệ & AI, trường học có nên dạy thêm ngoại ngữ.

segments.text: Why are some people better at learning languages than others?
Mhm, the first reason that comes to mind is that some people are naturally better at picking up new languages than others.
Take a friend of mine, for example.
He can remember new vocabulary really quickly, while I have to work much harder to remember the same words.
Another major reason could be that they're more passionate about learning languages.
So, they're willing to put more effort into it and spend more time practicing what they have learned.
As a result, they tend to improve much faster.
A lot of the time, people don't make as much progress as they could, simply because they don't practice often enough.
Is it easier for children to learn languages?
Yeah, I think so, especially when children are still very young.
They seem to pick up new sounds quite naturally.
They're also usually not as afraid of making mistakes as adults are, and that really matters when you're learning a new language.
Plus, children normally have fewer responsibilities, so they may have more time to learn and practice.
I guess that's why many parents these days send their children to English centers from an early age to take advantage of these benefits.
What is the best way to learn a foreign language?
I'm not an expert on language learning, but in my view, there isn't a one-size-fits-all method.
I think the best approach is to try different ways of learning and see what works best for you.
Take vocabulary, for example. Some people may pick up new words more easily by hearing them used in context or looking at pictures that illustrate the meanings,
while others may remember them for longer if they read them several times or write them down.
So, instead of looking for one magical solution, people should find a method that suits them and, more importantly, use it consistently.
Why do people learn foreign languages?
Well, as far as I'm concerned, people learn foreign languages for a variety of reasons, both personal and professional.
For one thing, knowing another language can make traveling abroad much easier because, like,
it enables people to communicate with locals and handle everyday situations more confidently.
For another, learning a foreign language can give people access to better job opportunities and increase their chances of landing a well-paid position.
These days, many companies prefer employees who can speak more than one language, especially if they work with international clients.
That's probably why a lot of people, particularly young people,
choose to spend their free time learning a new language, even if they aren't especially passionate about it.
Can technology help language learning?
Oh, 100%. I'd say technology has completely transformed the way people learn languages.
You know, in the past, it was much more challenging to become proficient in another language because people had fewer options.
I mean, they generally had to attend classes or even move to a country where they could use the language in everyday life.
These days, thanks to advances in technology, especially the recent development of AI, language learning has become much more accessible and convenient.
Besides attending classes in person, people can study online, use language learning apps, or even have conversations with AI chatbots.
This can save learners a great deal of time and money.
Should schools teach more foreign languages?
Ideally, yes, because we're living in an age when traveling and working abroad have become much more common than they were in the past.
That's why I think the more languages a person knows, the better.
I mean, being able to speak more than one language can open a lot of great opportunities.
That said, it might be difficult to make this happen in practice since, you know,
students already have to study a wide range of subjects at school.
If more languages were added to the curriculum, it could put even more pressure on them.
I think a better approach would be to offer additional languages as optional subjects.
So, students who are genuinely interested in them could choose to study them instead of making them compulsory for everyone.

sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 + 3 Band 8 samples: Describe an interesting video you watched on social media
title: Part 2: An interesting video you watched on social media
description: Video cô gái cổ vũ World Cup hóa ra do AI tạo: scrolling through Facebook, struck by how flawless she looked, at first glance, scams or misinformation.

segments.text: Describe an interesting video you watched on social media.
I have got to say, it took me a little while to think of one because I watch so many videos every day.
But, if I had to pick one that really stuck with me, I'd go for a video I saw a couple of weeks ago.
I remember I was scrolling through Facebook to unwind like I normally do,
when I came across a video of an incredibly attractive young woman sitting in the stands
and cheering for her national team, probably during a World Cup match.
I was immediately struck by how flawless she looked.
Out of curiosity, I went straight to the comment section to see how everyone else was reacting.
That was when I found out that the woman wasn't real and the whole video had been generated using AI.
Honestly, I couldn't believe it at first, so I watched it several more times to see if I could spot anything unusual.
What made it so interesting was just how realistic it looked.
Even though I'm quite familiar with technology, I couldn't tell that it was AI-generated at first glance.
You know, just 1 or 2 years ago,
people often make fun of AI videos because the characters' faces, hands, and movements looked obviously unnatural.
But now, some of them are so convincing that you have to pay close attention to little details to spot anything unusual.
At first, I was amazed by how rapidly AI technology has developed, but after thinking about it, I also felt a little worried.
I mean, if even someone my age can be fooled by a video like that,
older people might find it even harder to tell whether something is real or fake.
And that could become a serious problem if this technology is used for scams or misinformation.

sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 + 3 Band 8 samples: Describe an interesting video you watched on social media
title: Part 3: Online videos & social media
description: Video trực tuyến & mạng xã hội: comedy and educational content, AI-driven algorithms, a filter bubble, self-proclaimed experts, parental supervision, highly addictive.

segments.text: What types of videos are popular nowadays?
Mhm, it's hard to generalize because it really depends on people's interests, but comedy videos are probably among the most popular.
I guess the reason is quite simple.
They're highly entertaining, so watching them is a great way for people to unwind and clear their heads after a long day at work.
Another popular category is educational content.
Videos of this type often present useful information in a clear and visual way,
which makes them appealing to people who want to broaden their knowledge in different fields.
Do social media videos influence people's opinions?
From what I have seen, I'd definitely say so.
Most, if not all, social media platforms these days use AI-driven algorithms to recommend content based on users' interests and viewing habits.
As a result, once someone watches a particular video, they tend to be shown more similar content.
This can reinforce their existing beliefs and create a filter bubble, where they mainly see content they already agree with.
Over time, they may become more likely to believe one-sided or misleading information without really questioning it.
Are online videos educational? Yes, definitely.
There are many content creators online who are experts in their fields.
So, people can learn a great deal by watching their videos.
That said, there are also self-proclaimed experts who spread false or misleading information just to attract views.
This can make it difficult for viewers, especially those with little knowledge in a particular subject, to tell whether the information is reliable.
Do you think social media has more advantages than disadvantages?
I'd say the advantages probably outweigh the disadvantages, but it largely depends on how people use social media.
You know, social media in and of itself isn't necessarily harmful.
If people use it wisely, for example, by following educational content and keeping up with friends,
it can actually be a great tool for learning new things and staying connected with others.
However, if they become addicted to it and spend hours consuming mindless or toxic content,
it can have negative effects such as a shorter attention span and reduced productivity.
So, overall, I think if people use it responsibly, it will do more good than harm.
Should children's use of social media be controlled?
To some extent, yes. Children are generally quite impressionable, and many of them are not mature enough to exercise good judgment or clearly tell right from wrong.
Without proper parental supervision, they may be exposed to harmful content or become addicted to social media.
In the long run, this could lead to problems such as aggressive behavior, difficulty concentrating, or poor sleep.
That's why I think parents should control how much time their children spend on social media
and what type of content they are exposed to.
However, I don't think banning it completely would be necessary.
Why do people spend so much time watching videos online?
I think convenience is probably the biggest reason.
You know, nowadays, with the rise of smartphones and social media, people can gain instant access to online videos with just a few taps,
which makes it super easy to scroll from one video to the next.
Besides that, these videos, especially short-form ones, are designed to catch people's attention.
So, they tend to be highly addictive.
As a result, many people end up watching them for hours without even realizing it.

sourceTitle: IELTS PART 2 + 3 Band 8 Samples: Describe a perfect job you would like to have in the future
title: Part 2: A perfect job you would like to have in the future
description: Công việc mơ ước: online affiliate marketer — took off, tech-savvy, flexibility, a better work-life balance, build a name for myself, setbacks along the way.

segments.text: Describe a perfect job you would like to have in the future.
I've got to say that I'm quite satisfied with my current job, but if I had to choose another one,
I'd probably go for a career as an online affiliate marketer.
Actually, this type of work has become increasingly popular in recent years, especially since TikTok took off.
I think I first heard about it around 2 years ago when lots of people started talking about it on social media
and sharing how much money they had made from promoting products online.
As you might imagine, one of the most important skills required for this job is video editing.
You also need to know how to create engaging content and understand what your target audience is interested in.
It may sound a little complicated at first, particularly for people who aren't very tech-savvy,
but with enough patience and practice, I think almost anyone can learn how to do it.
The main reason why working as an online affiliate marketer would be my ideal job is the flexibility it offers.
It would give me much more control over my working hours
because I'd be the one who decides when to work and how to get everything done.
You know, I'm not someone who enjoys sitting in an office all day,
so this kind of job would give me the freedom to achieve a better work-life balance.
This would become especially important once I started a family and had children.
On top of that, if things went well, I could earn a good income and possibly build a name for myself online.
Of course, just like any other job, there would be difficulties and setbacks along the way.
Now that more and more people are interested in this line of work, the competition is becoming much more intense.
Even so, I'd still like to give it a shot and see how far I could go.

sourceTitle: IELTS PART 2 + 3 Band 8 Samples: Describe a perfect job you would like to have in the future
title: Part 3: Dream jobs
description: Nghề mơ ước của trẻ em và người lớn: meaningful and respected, attracted to fame, prestige, see life through rose-colored glasses, don't have what it takes.

segments.text: What types of jobs do children usually want to do?
It's hard to generalize because it really depends on a child's personality and interests,
but there are a few jobs that seem to be particularly popular.
For example, many children dream of becoming doctors, teachers, or police officers because they see these jobs as meaningful and respected.
Others may want to become singers, actors, or professional athletes because they're attracted to fame and the idea of doing something exciting.
These days, some children may even dream of becoming YouTubers or content creators because of what they see on social media.
So, their choices are often influenced by both their personal interests and the people they look up to.
What are the dream jobs of people in your country?
In the past, I'd say becoming a doctor or teacher was among the most common dream jobs
because these professions were seen as noble and highly respected.
However, in recent years, with the rise of social media, things have changed quite a lot.
Many people, especially younger ones, now dream of becoming content creators such as YouTubers or TikTokers because this kind of work offers great flexibility,
a better work-life balance, and the chance to earn a good income or even become famous.
As a result, these kinds of jobs have become increasingly popular.
Why do some jobs attract more people than others?
The first reason that comes to mind is salary.
Some jobs are simply more attractive because they pay much better than others.
And for most people, earning a good income is one of the main priorities when choosing a career.
Another factor is probably social status.
You know, jobs in fields like medicine, law, or senior management are often highly respected.
So, people may be drawn to them because of the prestige that comes with them.
Besides that, jobs that offer more stability, better working conditions, or clearer opportunities for promotion tend to attract more applicants, as well.
Why do people choose the job they mentioned as their dream job?
Hmm, that's a tricky one.
I guess one of the main reasons is that the job suits their interests, strengths, or even their personality.
For example, someone who enjoys helping others may dream of becoming a doctor or a teacher,
while someone who is more creative may want to work in design or content creation.
Of course, practical things like salary, job security, and future career opportunities also matter.
So, when a job is, how should I put it, both personally rewarding and offers a stable future,
people are naturally more likely to see it as their dream job.
Why do people change their dream jobs as they grow older?
From what I have seen, there are quite a few reasons for this,
but one of the most common is that people become more practical and realistic as they grow older.
You know, when we're kids, we tend to see life through rose-colored glasses, but later on,
we may realize that we simply don't have what it takes to turn those dreams into reality.
Take becoming a singer, for example.
Many people dreamed of singing on stage and having millions of fans when they were little,
but they eventually gave up on that dream when they realized that they didn't have a strong enough voice or the talent needed to succeed.
Another possible reason is that people's interests and priorities change over time.
So, a job they once considered perfect may no longer appeal to them.

sourceTitle: IELTS Speaking Part 2 + 3 Band 8 Samples: Describe a person who is good at planning things
title: Part 2: A person who is good at planning things
description: Cô bạn thân giỏi lên kế hoạch: we go way back, a daily to-do list, disciplined and punctual, on the spur of the moment, procrastination, a better version of myself.

segments.text: Describe a person who you think is good at planning things.
I'm going to talk about my best friend Yen, who is probably one of the most organized people I've ever known.
We live in the same neighborhood and we go way back.
I think I first met her when we were still very little and we've been through many ups and downs together.
Anyway, one thing you should know about her is that she has a good habit of planning ahead.
She usually spends some time early in the morning or the night before making a daily to-do list
and deciding what to prioritize so she can keep track of all her tasks.
And she's been doing so for many years now.
Because of that, she's pretty disciplined and punctual.
I've almost never seen her show up late for anything, whether it's a formal event or just a casual hangout.
Thanks to this habit, she's achieved a lot academically and I really admire her for that.
You know, last year she got a 7.5 in the IELTS exam even though she was still in grade 10.
You know, I'm the complete opposite.
I'm more of a spontaneous person and usually do things on the spur of the moment or leave things to the last minute.
That's why every now and then we have some arguments about my procrastination.
But deep down, I know she just wants me to become a better version of myself.
That said, recently I've started trying to break my bad habit by writing down the most important thing I need to finish each day.
And as you may have guessed, that's partly because of her encouragement and positive influence.
Sometimes I feel so lucky to have a great friend like her, and I hope our friendship will last no matter what happens.

sourceTitle: IELTS Speaking Part 2 + 3 Band 8 Samples: Describe a person who is good at planning things
title: Part 3: Why do people make plans?
description: Lập kế hoạch: casual plans vs bigger plans, once-in-a-lifetime occasions, go with the flow, career planning, give them an edge, blindly follow their advice.

segments.text: What types of plans do people often make with friends and family?
Well, people make all sorts of plans with their friends and family, but I'd say they usually fall into two main categories.
The first one is just casual plans like grabbing coffee, eating out, or watching a movie together.
For these kinds of plans, people only need to sort out basic details like where to meet and what time to show up.
The second type would be bigger plans, especially things like family trips, weekend getaways, or special celebrations.
These usually require a lot more thought because they involve money, transport, accommodation, and everyone's schedule.
So, people have to plan things properly to avoid last-minute problems and make sure the whole experience goes smoothly.
Is it important for people to plan special events such as weddings?
Oh yeah, no doubt about that.
Special events, especially weddings, are usually once-in-a-lifetime occasions.
So careful planning is absolutely essential.
You know, there are so many things to take care of from the venue and guest list to catering and decorations.
If something goes wrong, it doesn't just affect the couple themselves.
It can also put pressure on both families or even reflect badly on the people involved.
So, I'd say having a detailed plan is crucial if people want the event to run smoothly.
Honestly, I'd be quite surprised if someone had a wedding without planning things properly beforehand.
Why don't some people like to plan their social life in advance?
I guess one main reason is that some people are not really planners.
They're more of the spontaneous type.
They prefer to act on impulse and go with the flow instead of following a fixed schedule, which they might find boring or restrictive.
For them, planning everything in advance can take away the fun of spontaneity,
especially when it comes to social activities where the whole point is to relax and enjoy the moment.
I'm like that sometimes myself to be honest.
What are the advantages for young people of planning their future careers?
The first major benefit that comes to mind is that young people can have like a clearer sense of what steps they need to take.
If they have a career plan, they can prepare themselves better by getting relevant qualifications, building work experience, or improving their soft skills.
This can increase their chances of landing a well-paid job with good benefits and climbing the career ladder in the long run.
For example, if someone wants to become an English teacher in the future,
having qualifications like IELTS or TOEFL along with some teaching experience would definitely give them an edge over other candidates.
Should young people ask for advice about career planning, for example, from teachers or family?
Yeah, to some extent I think young people should definitely seek advice from teachers and family members because they often know them quite well.
You know, teachers may understand their academic strengths and weaknesses while parents usually have more life experience
and a better understanding of which careers might be stable or realistic.
That said, young people shouldn't blindly follow their advice either.
Sometimes parents in particular may push their children towards high-paying or prestigious jobs without considering whether they are genuinely interested in those fields.
So I think career advice is useful but at the end of the day young people still need to make their own decisions
because no one understands their interests and ambitions better than they do.
Do you agree or disagree that it is only possible to have a successful career if it has been carefully planned?
Well, in my view, that's often the case, but not always.
I do think careful planning can give people a clear direction and help them prepare for future opportunities.
However, I wouldn't say it's the only way to build a successful career.
You know, some careers, particularly in creative fields like art, music, or content creation, require a great deal of imagination and flexibility.
In those areas, it's hard to plan everything out in advance because the best ideas
or unexpected chances can sometimes come when people least expect them.
So overall, while planning is definitely important, I don't think it's the only path to success.

sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 + 3 Band 8 Samples: Describe a child you know who enjoys painting and drawing
title: Part 2: A child you know who enjoys painting or drawing
description: Cháu trai 8 tuổi mê vẽ: a real passion for art, portraits, natural landscapes, sharpen his skills, you should see the look on his face.

segments.text: Describe a child you know who enjoys painting or drawing.
Well, this immediately reminds me of my nephew, he's my older brother's first son,
and he has a real passion for art, especially drawing.
He's about 8 years old now and when you walk into his bedroom, you can instantly tell how much he loves drawing.
You know, the walls are covered with all kinds of drawings he has created and honestly they look amazing for a boy his age.
He can draw a wide range of things from animated characters and animals to portraits,
but I guess his favorite subjects are probably natural landscapes because I've seen lots of them in his sketchbooks.
Needless to say, he spends most of his free time drawing and according to his parents,
he can do it for hours without getting bored.
He's also into watching art-related videos on social media.
I once asked his parents when he started this hobby
and they told me it began quite early when he was still around 3 years old.
Yeah, you heard that right, 3 years old.
I was honestly amazed when I first heard it.
Anyway, after his parents noticed his talent, they sent him to art classes to help him like sharpen his skills
and he's been learning proper drawing techniques since then.
I don't often visit him because my brother and I live quite far from each other.
So, I can only go to his house a few times a year,
but whenever I do, I usually buy him some drawing tools as gifts.
And you should see the look on his face when he receives them.
It's pure happiness. I don't know if he's going to become an artist one day, but hopefully he can keep this passion for as long as possible.

sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 + 3 Band 8 Samples: Describe a child you know who enjoys painting and drawing
title: Part 3: Children, art & painting
description: Trẻ em và hội họa: fine motor skills, creativity and imagination, express their thoughts, galleries and museums, free admission days, only to a certain extent.

segments.text: At what age do children usually start to paint and draw?
Well, I'm not a parent yet, but from what I've seen, children usually start drawing or painting when they're around like three or four.
At that age, their fine motor skills are developing, so they can hold crayons or brushes and make simple shapes,
even if their drawings are still quite messy.
Also, children at that age tend to pick up new things really quickly.
So, I suppose it's a good time for them to explore creative activities like drawing and painting.
Should children have art lessons or classes at school?
Yes, definitely. I think art lessons are important because they help children develop their creativity and imagination.
You know, in an art class, children have to choose colors, shapes, and images by themselves, and they learn to turn their ideas into something visual.
For example, if they're asked to draw their dream house, a child may come up with a completely different version.
On top of that, art gives children a way to express their thoughts and feelings, especially when they can't put them into words.
Why do children often paint and draw more than adults do?
Hmm, that's an interesting question.
I guess one of the biggest reasons is that children are at an age when they still have plenty of time to explore their interests.
Adults, on the other hand, tend to have more hectic schedules and other responsibilities such as financial pressure and family matters.
So, it's harder for them to find time for artistic activities.
Another reason is that children are less afraid of being judged.
I mean, even if their drawings are messy, people usually see them as cute or creative,
whereas adults may feel embarrassed if their artwork doesn't look good.
So, children are more willing to experiment with painting and drawing.
Why do many people enjoy going to galleries and museums to see art?
Hmm, to tell you the truth, I'm not really one of those people, but I can see why others enjoy it.
You know, galleries and museums display artworks from different artists and historical periods.
So, art lovers can explore like a wide range of styles in one place.
Also, seeing a painting or a sculpture in real life feels very different from looking at it on a screen.
You can notice the colors, details, and textures more clearly, which makes the experience more special.
Should entry to galleries and museums be free for everyone?
No, I don't think entry should be completely free for everyone.
At the end of the day, galleries and museums need money to maintain their facilities,
upgrade their exhibitions, and provide a better experience for visitors.
If admission were free all the time, many of these places might struggle financially or even find it hard to stay open.
I think a better approach would be to offer free admission days or discounted tickets from time to time
so that people from low-income backgrounds still have a chance to visit.
Do you agree or disagree that when people look at art in galleries or museums, they can learn a lot about life in general?
Well, I partly agree, but I wouldn't say people can learn a lot about life just by looking at art.
You know, it's true that artworks can reflect many aspects of life such as love, war, poverty, or human relationships.
However, not everyone can understand the message or the story behind a painting, especially if they find art abstract or complicated.
On top of that, life is such a broad subject.
So, it's pretty hard to understand it through art alone.
So overall I think art can give people some insight into life but only to a certain extent.

sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 + 3 Band 8 Samples: Describe a time when you felt proud of a family member
title: Part 2: A time you felt proud of a family member
description: Tự hào khi anh trai đậu cùng lúc hai trường đại học: exploded with joy and pride, it was a blast, blood, sweat, and tears, a role model to me.

segments.text: Describe a time when you felt proud of a family member.
I'm going to talk about the time I received the news that my older brother got accepted into two universities at the same time, which made me feel extremely proud.
His name is Tim and he's 4 years older than me.
Although it happened a while ago, I still remember it vividly, almost as if it were just yesterday.
I was in my room scrolling through social media when I heard my parents screaming excitedly.
I quickly rushed out of my room to see what was going on and that's when I heard the news.
Needless to say, at that moment, all of us exploded with joy and pride.
My parents couldn't hide their happiness and they immediately told my relatives about it.
We threw a party later that night and it was a blast.
As for me, I not only took great pride in him, but also felt super happy for him.
It was, you know, a well-deserved reward for his years of blood, sweat, and tears.
You know what? To achieve this kind of success, he had put a lot of effort into his studies.
I remember when he was in secondary school, he was only an average student and it all changed after he entered high school.
He spent at least 4 hours a day on self-study and apart from attending classes at school,
he also took some extra classes to like improve his knowledge.
On top of that, he stayed away from video games, which many students are addicted to at that age.
His hard work was an inspiring example for me.
As a matter of fact, what he did gave me strong motivation to study hard and thanks to that,
I also made it to university with good grades.
Gosh, I really admire him and he's honestly like a role model to me.
Hopefully, one day I can be as hard working and successful as him.

sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 + 3 Band 8 Samples: Describe a time when you felt proud of a family member
title: Part 3: Pride, rewards & children
description: Khen thưởng & niềm tự hào: feel seen and supported, too much of a good thing, take them for granted, strike a balance, don't set the bar too high.

segments.text: When would parents feel proud of their children?
Well, as a parent myself, I'd say parents usually feel proud whenever their children achieve an important goal,
especially one that takes a lot of time and effort, like getting a high IELTS band score, for example.
You know, it's often the result of years of hard work and practice,
so it means a lot not only to the child, but also to the whole family.
In fact, I've read in the news that some families even hold a party to celebrate the day their children receive a good band score,
which really says a lot about how proud parents can feel.
Should parents reward children? Why and how?
Mhm, I've got to say this is quite a controversial topic in parenting, but personally,
I do think parents should reward their children, especially when they achieve something meaningful.
I mean, as human beings, we all want some recognition for our hard work, and children are no exception.
If that recognition comes from their parents, it carries even more emotional value, because it makes children feel seen and supported.
It can motivate them to keep pushing themselves, and more importantly,
it shows them that their parents are always there for them every step of the way.
And the reward doesn't have to be anything expensive.
It could simply be a family meal, a small gift, or even a few words of praise.
Is it good to reward children too often?
No, not really. In my view, too much of a good thing can be harmful.
You know, if children are showered with rewards all the time,
they may start to take them for granted and stop seeing them as something meaningful.
So, I think parents should be more selective when it comes to rewarding their kids.
For minor achievements, like finishing a LEGO set or getting a good mark in class,
a simple compliment or a few words of encouragement would be enough.
Bigger rewards should be saved for more meaningful milestones so children can truly appreciate them.
What do you think about children working hard just for grades?
Well, I wouldn't say it's necessarily a bad thing because after all,
doing well at school is what many parents and teachers expect from children and grades are probably the clearest way to measure that.
Plus, getting good grades does take a lot of effort so it's not something we should look down on.
That said, it can become a problem if children study only for grades.
You know, they may lose their natural curiosity and stop learning things deeply.
They may just memorize information for exams instead of actually understanding it.
Also, grades mainly show how well students perform in academic settings, whereas in real life,
practical skills can be just as important if not more important.
So, I think the better approach is to strike a balance.
What would children do to make their parents proud?
I don't know about other parents, but personally, I don't set the bar too high when it comes to this.
It may sound a bit cliche, but as long as my children grow up to be healthy,
kind and decent people, I'd already consider that a success.
That said, children can make their parents proud in many different ways.
It could be something as simple as behaving well at home or treating people around them with respect
or something bigger like achieving great academic results or reaching an important personal goal.
On what occasions would adults be proud of themselves?
It's hard to generalize because it varies greatly from person to person, but for the most part,
I'd say adults tend to feel proud of themselves when they achieve something meaningful or reach an important milestone in life.
This could be anything from finally getting rid of a bad habit to being able to afford something they've always dreamed of,
like a car or a house of their own.
For some people, it could even be something less visible,
like becoming more financially independent or building a stable career after years of hard work.

sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 + 3 Band 8 Samples: Describe a time when you weren't allowed to use your phone
title: Part 2: A time you weren't allowed to use your phone
description: Một tháng học quân sự không được dùng điện thoại: glued to my phone, "1 month in hell", improve my focus, bond with other students — hóa ra lại rất đáng nhớ.

segments.text: Describe an occasion when you were not allowed to use your mobile phone.
I got to say it took me a while to come up with one experience
because nowadays my phone is always in my pocket whether I'm at home or out and about.
Anyway, I'm going to talk about the time when I took part in a military course at my university.
If I remember correctly, it happened quite a few years ago back when I was still like a first-year student.
At the time, I just finished all my final exams and as part of my university curriculum,
I had to go to a military camp with other students for a month.
We had to stay in a building inside the camp during the week and could only go home on weekends.
The worst thing was that I wasn't allowed to use my phone during any of the training sessions.
And these sessions took up almost the whole day every day.
Back then, I was basically glued to my phone.
So, when I first heard about the rules, I was like, "Oh boy, it's going to be 1 month in hell."
But, I was completely wrong.
It turned out to be one of the most unforgettable experiences I've ever had.
Without my phone, I had no choice but to pay attention to my lecturers and that unexpectedly helped me improve my focus in class.
On top of that, the course included many outdoor and group activities.
So, it gave me a chance to bond with other students.
During breaks, instead of taking out my phone and browsing Facebook like I usually did,
I spent time talking to other students and ended up making lots of new friends.
Honestly, I don't think any of these things would have happened if I had been allowed to use my phone freely.
That experience made me realize that being away from my phone for a while wasn't as terrible as I had imagined.

sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 + 3 Band 8 Samples: Describe a time when you weren't allowed to use your phone
title: Part 3: Mobile phones: friendship, photos & laws
description: Điện thoại di động: người trẻ vs người già, ảnh hưởng đến tình bạn, chụp ảnh có phí thời gian không, có cần luật không — và khi điện thoại khiến ta khó chịu (downright disrespectful).

segments.text: How do young and old people use mobile phones differently?
It's hard to generalize because it varies greatly from person to person.
But overall, I think it's safe to say that young people tend to use their phones for a wider range of purposes.
Whether it's for entertainment, studying, working, or even making money.
They're usually more tech-savvy, so they can make the best use of their phones.
Older people, by contrast, mainly use their phones for, you know, keeping in touch with family and friends, or watching videos on social media.
That said, recently, I feel like older people have become more comfortable with technology.
So, some of them also spend time scrolling through social media, just like many young adults do.
What positive and negative impact do mobile phones have on friendship?
Well, on the upside, mobile phones make it much easier for friends to stay in touch.
You know, nowadays, thanks to smartphones, we can chat, send voice messages, or even make video calls every day,
which was something we could never have imagined in the past.
However, on the downside, these devices can also reduce face-to-face interaction and weaken real-life connections.
I've seen many cases where a group of friends get together at a cafe,
but each of them is glued to their phones instead of actually talking to each other, which is quite ironic.
Is it a waste of time to take pictures with mobile phones?
No, I don't think so.
Pictures, no matter what you use to take them, help people capture beautiful moments in their lives.
So, they can look back and reminisce about them later on.
So, I don't think it's a waste of time at all.
In fact, for me, it's one of the best aspects of mobile phones.
You know, they allow people to preserve memories.
I guess it only becomes a waste of time when people take pictures too often or too mindlessly without any real meaning behind them.
Do you think it is necessary to have laws on the use of mobile phones?
Well, in theory, it may sound like a good idea, but in reality,
I don't think it's very practical because, you know, phones are personal devices.
So, people should be free to use them as they wish.
I think a better approach would be to run awareness campaigns to help people understand the negative effects of spending too much time on their phones and how to use them more wisely.
That way, they can make more informed choices when it comes to, like, using mobile phones.
Many people think mobile phones can be annoying at times.
Can you give any examples of that?
Oh, yeah, I completely agree with that.
Especially when you're talking to someone, but they're on their phone the whole time and completely tuned out.
I don't know about other people, but for me, it's downright disrespectful.
I mean, what's the point of seeing each other face-to-face if you don't even care enough to look at me while I'm talking to you, right?
Another common example is when you're trying to explain something to someone, but they get distracted by their phone,
don't pay enough attention, and then end up asking you to explain it again. I really hate that.

sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 + 3 Band 8 Samples: Describe an unusual meal you had
title: Part 2: An unusual meal you had
description: Bữa buffet có thịt cá sấu ở resort Cam Ranh: caught me off guard, going back and forth in my head, nothing to write home about, bizarre.

segments.text: Describe an unusual meal you had.
Well, I've been lucky enough to try quite a few good meals, but if I had to pick out one that really stood out as unusual,
it would probably be this buffet I had on a family trip.
If I remember correctly, it was just last year when we went to Cam Ranh, a beautiful coastal area in southern Vietnam.
We stayed there for like 3 days and 2 nights at a beachfront resort called Selectum Noa.
And you know what? They actually offered like five meals a day, so we were basically eating nonstop.
There was a huge variety of food ranging from local Vietnamese dishes to international ones.
But the one thing that really caught me off guard was this section with, you know, alligator meat.
I think they were probably baby alligators because they still had their heads and jaws on display.
And they looked quite small compared to what I'd imagined.
Honestly, I was kind of shocked when I saw them.
I was like, wait, do people actually eat this?
Because I'd always assumed it might be illegal or something.
At first, I was really hesitant.
I mean, I'm not the kind of person who eats wild animals, so I was kind of going back and forth in my head.
But then I thought, you know what?
When am I ever going to get this chance again?
So I just went for it and took a small bite.
And to be honest, it was just fine.
Nothing special, nothing to write home about.
What made this meal particularly bizarre for me wasn't just the food itself, but the whole experience.
You know, having a buffet like that with my family in a luxury resort isn't something I get to do very often.
So I think that's what made it so memorable.

sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 + 3 Band 8 Samples: Describe an unusual meal you had
title: Part 3: Eating out, fast food & food culture
description: Ăn ngoài, đồ ăn nhanh và văn hóa ẩm thực Việt: order in, promo codes, it boils down to…, the social side of things, banh mi, triggered a lot of backlash.

segments.text: What are the advantages and disadvantages of eating in restaurants?
Well, one major benefit is that you get to enjoy a wide variety of dishes that are,
you know, professionally prepared, which is something you probably can't easily make at home.
Plus, restaurants usually have a really nice atmosphere, so they're perfect for things like dates or special occasions.
But on the flip side, it can be quite expensive, especially if you eat out regularly.
So, it's not always affordable for everyone.
Do people eat fast food at home?
Yeah, especially in this day and age with the rise of food delivery apps,
people tend to order in a lot more often than in the past.
And fast food is no exception.
I guess it's mainly because this kind of food is really convenient and is also easy to clean up afterwards.
Plus, with auto discount programs and promo codes, you can sometimes get it cheaper than eating at a restaurant.
Why do some people choose to eat out instead of ordering takeout?
I guess it boils down to the fact that they're not just looking for food, but for something more than that.
I'm talking about the social side of things like seeing other people,
being in a nice environment, or having someone to talk to while enjoying a meal.
Those are things that ordering takeout simply can't replace.
That's probably why eating out is often preferred for things like catching up or celebrating special occasions.
Do people in your country socialize in restaurants?
Yeah, it's actually one of the most common ways for Vietnamese people to socialize.
If you go to any restaurant, especially in the evening or on weekends, it's usually packed with people regardless of age or gender.
I think many people like it because of the overall experience it offers.
I mean, they can have good food while catching up with others.
And sometimes, especially when it comes to more upscale restaurants, people can also enjoy excellent service, a lively atmosphere, and beautifully designed spaces.
What kinds of fast food are there in your country?
I think just like in many other countries, there's a wide range of fast food available here in Vietnam.
But one that enjoys a great popularity is probably burgers.
You know, they're quick and easy to eat, kind of like banh mi.
So, they appeal to a lot of people.
Another common option would be pizza.
The fact that there are so many pizza places around the city already speaks volumes about how popular it is.
Do people in your country value food culture?
Sorry, what do you mean by food culture?
Do you mean things like traditional dishes and eating habits?
Yes. If so, then I'd say it's definitely valued in Vietnam.
We take great pride in our traditional dishes like pho or banh mi.
Actually, just recently there was a Vietnamese girl who posted a short video on social media,
kind of putting banh mi down, and it quickly triggered a lot of backlash from people across the country.
I think that really speaks volumes.
If that doesn't show how much we value our food culture, I don't know what does.

sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 + 3: Describe a positive change that you have made in your daily life recently
title: Part 2: A positive change you made in your daily life
description: Thay đổi tích cực: bỏ thức khuya, đi ngủ sớm dậy sớm — a night owl, fight a mental battle, the snooze button, sluggish, absolutely stoked.

segments.text: Describe a positive change that you have made in your daily life recently.
I'm going to talk about my new habit of going to bed early and getting up early every day,
which is a big change from my old routine.
I decided to make this change just a few months ago because my health was starting to decline.
You know, I'd been a night owl for years and my body began to show some negative effects.
I mean, I had a lot of pimples, I often forgot things and I found it hard to focus for long periods.
On top of that, I always felt like drained and a bit grumpy in the morning.
That's when it hit me that I really needed to change and make an effort to stick with it.
But honestly, when it comes to breaking a long-standing habit, it's not as easy as it sounds.
I remember in the first week, I kept falling back into my old routine of staying up late
and I had to fight a mental battle just to get out of bed on time without hitting the snooze button.
As a result, I felt extremely sleepy and sluggish and needed a caffeine boost to get through the day.
But after about like 3 weeks of consistent effort, it finally became a habit.
Needless to say, I was absolutely stoked because I always thought I was naturally a night person and couldn't change that.
Now I go to bed at 10:00 p.m. and wake up at like 5:30 almost every day, which is a huge improvement.
Thanks to that, I have more time during the day and my productivity has improved a lot.
I get more work done and just feel more alive overall.
I guess in the future, I'll try to break other bad habits so I can become even more productive.

sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 + 3: Describe a positive change that you have made in your daily life recently
title: Part 3: Changing habits & routines
description: Thói quen & thay đổi: taking a toll on their health, mindlessly scrolling, peer pressure, short-lived motivation, quit cold turkey, small consistent changes.

segments.text: Why do people want to change their routines?
As someone who has done that several times before, I think one of the main reasons is that people find their routines unhealthy.
For example, they may have a habit of staying up late and it's kind of taking a toll on their overall health.
So, they feel the need to change.
Another major reason is related to productivity.
Maybe they waste a lot of time on unimportant things and they want to improve themselves.
So, they're determined to adjust their routine.
Yeah, those are the two main reasons I can think of for now.
Is it difficult to change daily habits?
Well, I don't know about others, but for me, it can be quite hard to change daily habits,
especially when it comes to habits you have had for years.
I mean, once something becomes part of your daily routine, it's really challenging to break out of it,
even if you know it's not good for you.
Take me for example. I've been trying to cut down on my screen time lately, but I still catch myself,
you know, mindlessly scrolling on my phone without even realizing it.
And afterwards, I kind of feel guilty, like I should have been doing something more productive instead.
Do young people change their routines more often?
Well, yeah, I'd say so.
Young people are still at a stage where they're like trying to figure things out, so their routines are naturally more flexible.
They tend to try out different lifestyles or habits just to see what suits them best.
Plus, they're easily influenced by trends or social media,
so it's quite common for them to adjust their routines from time to time based on what they see online.
By contrast, older people usually have more responsibilities, so they prefer to stick to a stable routine.
What motivates people to make positive changes?
Well, I suppose there are quite a few factors, but one of the main ones is probably exposure to inspirational content.
People might come across it in books, online articles,
or on social media and it can give them a strong boost of motivation to like take action right away.
That said, this kind of motivation is often short-lived and tends to fade after a while.
Another big factor is peer pressure and the desire to keep up with others.
You know, when people see those around them, especially someone their age,
achieving something in life, they are more likely to push themselves to do better.
And sometimes the motivation does come from within.
People simply want to improve their lives.
How long does it take to form a new habit?
I don't think there's a fixed answer to that.
It really depends on the person and the habit itself.
You know, some habits are easier to pick up, like drinking more water, while others, like waking up early, take more discipline and effort.
But for the most part, I'd say it can take a few weeks to a couple of months for a new habit to really stick, especially if people stay consistent with it.
Can small changes make a big difference?
Yeah, definitely. Many people assume that only big changes bring great results, but for me, it's the small steps that really go a long way.
A lot of the time, when it comes to building a new habit,
the idea of having to start big actually stops people from taking action.
I mean, you can't expect a smoker to quit cold turkey, right?
They usually have to gradually cut down on the number of cigarettes they smoke each day,
and over time, that can lead to a significant change in their behavior.
So, in many cases, it's the small, consistent changes that lead to long-term results.

sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 + 3 band 8 samples: Describe a program or app on your computer or phone
title: Part 2: A program or app on your computer or phone
description: ChatGPT — ứng dụng dùng mỗi ngày: a global phenomenon, handle everyday requests, a kind of therapist, get back on my feet, double-check things.

segments.text: Describe a program or app on your computer or phone.
Well, I got to say I use plenty of apps on my phone these days,
but if I had to pick one, I'd go for ChatGPT because I've been using it quite a lot lately.
I don't remember exactly when I downloaded it, but it must have been 1 or 2 years ago,
especially when it started becoming like a global phenomenon and everyone was talking about it.
As you probably know, it's an AI chatbot
and its main purpose is to help people look for information and handle everyday requests almost instantly.
I think I use it pretty much every day either on the website
or the app on my phone depending on what I'm doing at the time.
What makes it particularly useful to me is that it can help me with a wide range of things.
For example, I can use it to teach myself English, ask questions about topics I'm not familiar with,
or even edit and generate images for personal use.
It's also really helpful when it comes to, you know, checking information or translating something from a foreign language.
Believe it or not, sometimes when I feel a bit down or run into problems in life,
it can even act like a kind of therapist giving me useful advice to help me get back on my feet.
In a way, it's like a virtual friend of mine and has become part of my daily routine.
I guess the only thing I don't like about it is that at times the information it provides can be a bit inconsistent or inaccurate.
So, I usually need to double-check things carefully.
You know, ever since I started using it, I've learned a lot of great things to broaden my knowledge.
So, I feel quite grateful to the people who created it.

sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 + 3 band 8 samples: Describe a program or app on your computer or phone
title: Part 3: Are we too dependent on apps?
description: Ứng dụng điện thoại: convenience, designed to be addictive, take productivity up a notch, over-reliant, eye strain, social cohesion, parental guidance.

segments.text: Why do people use apps so frequently?
Well, I suppose it mostly comes down to convenience.
You know, nowadays almost everyone regardless of age has a smartphone, so they can instantly access different apps whenever they need.
On top of that, apps help us deal with like a wide range of things in daily life,
whether it's entertainment, studying, working, or even making money.
Another reason could be that many apps are designed to be quite addictive.
You know, with notifications and personalized content, so people keep coming back to them throughout the day.
So, yeah, that's probably why we tend to use them on a regular basis without even realizing it.
How do apps improve productivity?
I'd say apps have really taken our productivity up a notch.
You know, with the rise of AIs and all that,
these apps can help us handle a much heavier workload than we could in the past.
Especially when it comes to automating repetitive tasks like scheduling, reminders, or data entry,
which allows us to focus on more important or creative work.
Take creating documents, for example, with just a few simple steps, you can get apps to generate one in a matter of seconds.
That said, the downside is that we might become over-reliant on them.
And if that continues over time, our own skills could get a bit rusty.
Are people too dependent on digital apps?
Sadly, yeah. I think to some extent they are.
From what I have seen, lots of people, regardless of age or gender,
spend a huge chunk of their day on these apps, especially social media.
And you can easily notice that when you are out in public.
While these apps can improve our lives in many ways, they can also lead to negative consequences,
particularly when it comes to our health and real-life interactions, which I think is quite alarming.
What problems can apps cause?
Well, like I mentioned earlier, there are quite a few issues that come with using these apps.
In terms of health, they can make us less physically active
since we tend to spend a large portion of our time sitting and looking at screens.
In the long run, this might lead to some lifestyle-related issues such as neck pain, eye strain, or even more serious conditions.
On top of that, our attention span may be negatively affected making it harder for us to stay focused for, you know, extended periods of time.
Besides, people may become more socially isolated as they tend to interact through screens rather than face-to-face.
How do apps influence communication?
Mhm, off the top of my head, I'd say apps have both positive and negative impacts on the way we communicate.
On the one hand, they make everything a lot more convenient
and give us more options when it comes to keeping in touch with people around us.
For example, we can text, send voice messages, or even make video calls via messaging apps,
which is something we could have never imagined in the past.
But at the same time, they also reduce the amount of face-to-face interaction, which may weaken social cohesion in the long run.
Should children be allowed to use many apps?
Mhm, I don't know about others, but for me, children should be allowed to use some apps but only with parental guidance.
The main reason is that kids are quite impressionable.
So, they're not always mature enough to make good judgments or tell right from wrong.
That's why if we let them use apps freely, they may be exposed to, you know, harmful content which can actually backfire.

sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 + 3 band 8 Samples: Describe a person you know who runs a family business
title: Part 2: A person you know who runs a family business
description: Người dì mở tiệm tạp hóa gia đình ở quê: drop by, get it off the ground, relentless hard work, strong business sense, customer satisfaction.

segments.text: Describe a person you know who runs a family business.
I'm going to talk about my aunt who runs a family grocery store in my hometown.
Her name is Ang and she's in her 50s now.
I don't see her very often these days,
but I usually drop by her store during special occasions like Tet or whenever I'm back home from a long break.
To be honest, I'm not exactly sure when she first started the business,
but it must have been ages ago, probably even before I was born.
It's not a huge store or anything like that,
but it's well known locally and I think most people in my town have shopped there at least once.
The store sells a wide range of products from snacks and packaged food to everyday household items.
Just like any other business, her family-run store has gone through quite a few ups and downs over the years.
From what my mother told me, she actually started out with a very small shop and even had to borrow money from people around her,
you know, just to get it off the ground.
But thanks to her relentless hard work and like strong business sense, she's managed to keep it running and gradually expand it.
Now she even employs several staff members.
I think one of the main reasons why people keep coming back is the way she treats her customers.
You know, unlike some shop owners who can be a bit cold and impatient, she's incredibly friendly and welcoming.
She greets everyone with a smile and takes the time to ask what they need.
She also makes sure her staff provides same level of service because for her, customer satisfaction is the top priority.
So yeah, I really admire her and I just hope her business keeps growing in the future.

sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 + 3 band 8 Samples: Describe a person you know who runs a family business
title: Part 3: Family businesses
description: Doanh nghiệp gia đình — 9 câu hỏi Part 3: flexibility, conflicts become personal, follow in their parents' footsteps, close-knit, cost-effective.

segments.text: What are the advantages of running a family business?
Well, I haven't run a family business myself, so I'm not entirely sure, but from my perspective, one of the biggest advantages is flexibility.
You know, unlike working for a company, you don't have to follow strict rules or fixed office hours.
So, you can organize your schedule in a way that suits your lifestyle.
As a result, it can lead to a better work-life balance, especially if you value spending time with your family.
On top of that, since most of your colleagues are family members,
the working environment tends to be more comfortable and supportive compared to a typical corporate setting.
What challenges do family businesses face?
Well, I suppose there are quite a few challenges, but the first one that comes to mind is dealing with conflicts.
Since everyone involved is part of the same family, disagreements can easily become personal rather than professional.
As a result, even small problems at work can damage relationships and create long-term tension within the family.
Another major issue is the lack of professionalism in some cases.
For example, decisions might be based on emotions or family ties, rather than ability or experience.
This can lead to poor management or even affect the overall performance of the business in the long run.
Do young people prefer to work for family businesses or companies?
Mhm, I can't speak for everyone, but from what I've seen,
a lot of young people tend to prefer working for companies rather than family businesses.
I think one of the main reasons is that companies are usually more structured and professional,
especially when it comes to things like paperwork or management systems.
Also, there's often less bias in larger organizations,
so employees are more likely to be treated fairly and have equal opportunities for promotion or fringe benefits.
How can family relationships affect a business?
If we're talking about family-run businesses, I'd say family relationships can have a huge impact.
You know, if family members get along well and share the same goals, it can really help the business grow.
And it also creates a more supportive and comfortable working environment.
On the other hand, if there are conflicts or disagreements within the family,
it can lead to poor decision-making and even affect other employees over time.
Is it difficult to pass a family business to the next generation?
Oh, it can be quite challenging, to be honest.
Younger people nowadays often have different career goals, so they may not want to follow in their parents' footsteps.
Another thing is that running a business requires a lot of experience, so if they're not well prepared,
the business may struggle or, in the worst-case scenario, even shut down in the long run.
Are family businesses common in your country?
Yeah, I don't know about other countries, but in Vietnam, family businesses are quite common both in big cities and smaller towns.
I guess one reason for this is that they're usually easier to manage
and tend to offer more flexibility compared to larger, more professional companies.
What I mean by that is family members can make decisions more quickly
and they often have more control over their working hours, like when to take a day off.
That's probably why many people prefer this kind of business, especially if they value independence and a more comfortable working environment.
Why are family businesses popular in some countries?
I think one of the main reasons for this is because family values are strongly emphasized in some cultures.
You know, in many countries, people tend to trust their relatives more than outsiders,
so they feel more comfortable working together and building something as a family.
Also, in some places, starting a business with family members is simply more practical and cost-effective.
For example, you don't have to spend as much on hiring employees,
and family members are often more willing to make sacrifices, especially in the early stages of the business.
Do you think family businesses are better than large companies?
I think it really depends on what someone is looking for because both have their own advantages.
On the one hand, family businesses often offer a more supportive and close-knit working environment,
which can make people feel more comfortable and less stressed.
On the other hand, large companies tend to provide better career prospects and more opportunities for professional development.
So, overall, I wouldn't say one is better than the other.
It really comes down to personal preferences and long-term goals.
What skills are important for running a family business?
I'm not an expert in this, but the way I see it,
one of the most important skills is probably communication because you need to clearly separate work issues from personal relationships.
If people aren't careful, misunderstandings can quickly turn into, like, personal conflicts.
Another key skill would be leadership, especially the ability to make fair and objective decisions.
You know, even though you're working with family,
you still need to treat everyone equally and focus on what's best for the business rather than letting emotions take over.

sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 + 3 Band 8 Samples: Describe an occasion when you lost your way
title: Part 2: An occasion when you lost your way
description: Lạc đường khi đi xe máy đến Vũng Tàu vì tin Google Maps: let our hair down, the middle of nowhere, a dead end, in hindsight, what was bound to happen happened.

segments.text: Describe an occasion when you lost your way.
This immediately reminds me of a trip I took about 3 years ago when I was still a freshman student.
At that time, I just finished my university exams and my friends and I were like mentally exhausted.
So, we decided to go to Vung Tau to relax and, you know, just let our hair down for a few days.
It's a coastal city not too far from Ho Chi Minh City, only about 120 km away.
So, we thought, "Why not ride motorbike there?"
Back then, it sounded fun and adventurous.
The only problem was none of us had ever been there before.
So, naturally, we depended entirely on Google Maps.
It gave us three route options and without thinking twice, we chose the shortest one.
In hindsight, that was a terrible decision.
At first, everything was going perfectly.
The weather was nice, the road was smooth, and we were all in such a good mood.
Then, suddenly, the app told us to turn onto this tiny dirt road.
There was no street lights, no houses, no other vehicles.
It was basically the middle of nowhere.
I remember thinking, "This feels a bit off."
But, we kept going because we trusted the app blindly.
And then, what was bound to happen happened.
We hit a dead end and realized we were completely lost.
We'd been misled by the app.
In the end, we had to ride all the way back and ask some locals for directions,
which honestly, we should have done in the first place.
We arrived in Vung Tau later than expected, but thankfully, nothing serious happened.
Looking back, getting lost was actually one of the most memorable parts of the trip.
It made the whole experience feel more adventurous and now is something we still laugh about whenever we talk about that holiday.

sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 + 3 Band 8 Samples: Describe an occasion when you lost your way
title: Part 3: Maps, directions & getting lost
description: Bản đồ, chỉ đường và lạc đường: rely too heavily on, double-check, sense of direction, off the beaten path, wind up in…, navigation skills.

segments.text: Why do people still get lost despite modern technology?
I guess it mainly comes down to the fact that people these days rely too heavily on modern technology, even though navigation systems aren't always accurate.
You know, sometimes apps can give incorrect directions or certain places may have changed without being updated on the system.
If users don't double-check the information, they can easily end up getting lost.
And I'm actually a perfect example of that.
Also, I think people have gradually lost their sense of direction because they don't need to memorize routes anymore.
Is it better to ask people for directions or use maps?
Well, I'd probably lean more towards using maps, especially digital ones.
You know, they are much quicker and generally quite reliable.
All you have to do is type in the destination and within seconds, you'll be given several possible routes, which is really convenient.
Also, these days, almost everyone owns a smartphone and internet access is available almost everywhere.
So, using a map is usually the easiest option.
That said, I think asking locals can make sense in certain situations.
For example, if you're traveling in a remote or mountainous area where the signal is weak or the map hasn't been updated properly.
Honestly, I don't think a person's sense of direction really depends on their age.
I'd say it has more to do with how often they actually use it.
You know, if someone travels frequently and pays close attention to their surroundings instead of relying entirely on GPS,
their spatial awareness tends to improve over time.
So, it's completely possible for an older person to have a better sense of direction than a younger one, especially if they're constantly on the move.
And the reverse can also be true.
How has technology changed the way people travel?
I'd say technology has completely transformed the way people travel.
With the rise of GPS and navigation apps, getting around unfamiliar places has become much easier and more convenient.
People no longer have to worry as much about getting lost, which gives them more confidence to explore new destinations.
At the same time, online booking platforms allow travelers to organize their trips quickly and conveniently,
making traveling far more accessible than in the past.
Can getting lost sometimes be a positive experience?
Mhm, it can be positive in certain situations, especially when you unexpectedly discover some, you know, unspoiled natural spots.
Sometimes, getting lost allows you to explore places off the beaten path.
However, in most cases, I'd say it's more stressful than enjoyable
because it can delay your plans or even put you in an unsafe situation.
If you wind up in a place where there aren't many people around
and your GPS stops working, the situation can quickly become quite frightening.
I've actually experienced something like that myself.
Should children be taught navigation skills?
Yeah, I definitely think children should be taught navigation skills.
You know, in this day and age, with growing safety concerns like traffic accidents or even abductions,
it's increasingly important for kids to know how to find their way around independently.
It gives them a sense of confidence and reduces the risk of panic if they ever get separated from adults.
That said, I don't think it means they should rely entirely on technology.
Ideally, children should learn both traditional navigation skills and how to use digital tools responsibly so they can handle different situations more effectively.

sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 + 3 Band 8 Samples: Describe a music event that you didn't enjoy
title: Part 2: A music event you didn't enjoy
description: Một buổi diễn nhạc rock không như mong đợi: a small gig at a cafe, heavy metal, headbanging, too wild for me, not really my type of music.

segments.text: Describe a music event that you didn't enjoy.
Well, I have to admit that I rarely go to music events these days,
but I remember one time when I went to a live music performance with a friend of mine,
and unfortunately, I didn't really enjoy it that much.
Actually, it wasn't a big concert or anything like that, just a small gig at a cafe where several local rock bands were performing.
It happened a long time ago, back when I was still like a university student, so I don't remember all the details.
Forgive me, but I also forgot its name.
Though I do remember it was located in District 1, right in the heart of the city.
Back then, a friend of mine asked me to go there with him because,
you know, I had once told him that I was interested in rock music.
At first, everything seemed quite nice.
The cafe was decorated in a rock-themed style with guitars hanging on the walls and posters of famous rock bands.
It was filled with foreigners and rock music lovers, and many of them had long hair and painted their nails black.
However, when the music started and the first band went on stage, I kind of realized it wasn't really what I was expecting.
The kind of rock music they played was heavy metal, which, in case you didn't know,
is usually very loud and fast-paced with lots of screaming, so it was quite hard for me to understand the lyrics.
At some point, many people in the crowd even started headbanging, which felt a bit too wild for me.
That said, I still tried to stay for a while because my friend was really enjoying it.
On the bright side, that music gig helped me realize that heavy metal isn't really my type of music.

sourceTitle: IELTS SPEAKING PART 2 + 3 Band 8 Samples: Describe a music event that you didn't enjoy
title: Part 3: Concerts & live music
description: Sự kiện âm nhạc: the electric atmosphere, open-air concerts, music festivals, live vs recorded music, sound quality, performance fees.

segments.text: Why do people attend music events?
Well, I suppose one of the main reasons is that people love the electric atmosphere that these events offer.
I mean, when you're surrounded by thousands of fans singing along to the songs, it creates a real sense of connection,
which makes the whole experience much more exciting than just listening to music at home.
Another possible reason is that music events give people a chance to, you know,
socialize with their loved ones, and more importantly, see their favorite artists perform in person.
So, in a sense, it's not just about enjoying good music, but also about spending quality time together and creating lasting memories.
What kind of music events do people like today?
Well, it's hard to generalize because it really comes down to personal taste.
You know, some people love being out in the open air,
so they might opt for outdoor concerts like ones held at the beach
or on a hill where they can get close to nature and enjoy the music at the same time.
Others are more extroverted and enjoy high-energy environments, so they're more into music festivals where they can be part of a massive crowd.
Then there are also people who prefer something more intimate,
so they might choose to attend a small gig at a cafe or a bar instead.
Are live performances better than recorded music?
Well, it really depends on the artist, but most of the time, I'd say it's the other way around.
You know, recorded songs are usually carefully edited and polished,
